meta.statement:
Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold, and let $\theta$ be a smooth
closed real $(1,1)$-form such that $\operatorname{PSH}(X,\theta)\ne\varnothing$.
Write

$$
\mathscr D_{\mathcal I}(X,\theta)
:=\operatorname{PSH}(X,\theta)/{\sim_{\mathcal I}}
$$

for the set of *realizable* $\mathcal I$-data. Thus an element is induced by
an actual $\varphi\in\operatorname{PSH}(X,\theta)$ and is represented by the
tower $(\mathcal I(m\varphi))_{m\ge1}$, equivalently by its divisorial Lelong
profile; it is not an arbitrary formal sequence of ideals. For
$d=[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}$, define

$$
\mathcal R_\theta(d):=P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}.
$$

**Theorem (P14.8 v5).**

1. The map $\mathcal R_\theta$ is well defined and returns the unique
   normalized $\mathcal I$-model potential in the class $d$. Hence full
   realizable $\mathcal I$-data reconstructs its canonical normalized
   $\mathcal I$-model representative, with no hypothesis on nonpluripolar
   mass.

2. Raw nonpluripolar mass is not part of $\mathcal I$-data. On
   $X=\mathbf P^1$, equipped with the Fubini--Study form $\omega$ normalized
   by $\int_X\omega=1$, there is one $\mathcal I$-class containing potentials
   $\varphi_s$, $0\le s\le1$, such that

   $$
   [\varphi_s]_{\mathcal I}=[0]_{\mathcal I},\qquad
   \int_X\left\langle\omega+\operatorname{dd}^c\varphi_s\right\rangle=1-s.
   $$

   In particular, the raw zero-mass representative $\varphi_1$ has canonical
   normalized $\mathcal I$-model representative $0$, whose mass is one. So
   neither a raw zero-mass representative nor its mass can be reconstructed
   from its $\mathcal I$-class.

These settle the two defined readings of the former P14.8 wording: complete
realizable $\mathcal I$-data determines the canonical normalized
$\mathcal I$-model representative, while neither a raw representative nor
its raw mass descends to the $\mathcal I$-quotient.

**Scope.** On a smooth projective variety, the separate all-mass order
isomorphism for full realized DXZ--Boucksom--Jonsson objects in a
pseudoeffective real Néron--Severi class remains distinct. The literal
all-semivaluation ideal formula is used only for a $\mathbf Q$-line-bundle
class. This theorem asserts neither a compact-Kähler nor a genuinely
transcendental extension of that result. Realization of arbitrary formal
ideal or valuative data remains P14.1, and the P14.7 terminal-left-limit
corollary is not used here.

The exact source excerpts used by the proof are appended to its frozen V6
packet: Boucksom's multiplier-ideal notes, BEGZ's nonpluripolar-product
paper, and Kellay--Mashreghi, arXiv:1102.5596, formula (3.4), for the
generalized-Cantor capacity criterion.

record.location: Proof, first paragraph defining F_d
record.detail: For an actual representative phi, compactness and upper semicontinuity make sup_X phi finite, and phi-sup_X phi is theta-psh, nonpositive, and has unchanged multiplier ideals, so F_d is nonempty. Finite maxima of theta-psh functions are theta-psh and remain nonpositive. At every prime divisor over X the generic Lelong number of a maximum is the minimum; because both inputs have the same profile d, the maximum has that same profile. The divisorial criterion therefore keeps the entire scaled multiplier-ideal tower fixed, so F_d is directed under finite maxima.

record.location: Proof, paragraph beginning 'Put U' through equation nu(U,E)=lim_j nu(u_j,E)
record.detail: The family is locally uniformly bounded above by zero, so Choquet's lemma produces a countable subfamily whose supremum has the same usc regularization U. Finite successive maxima u_j stay in F_d, increase, and converge almost everywhere to U. For any fixed prime divisor E on a model, Lemma 10.5 permits one point of E outside the countable union of exceptional analytic sets for all pulled-back u_j and U. After adding a smooth local potential for the pulled-back theta, these are local psh functions; the increasing-limit Lelong theorem applies and yields nu_E(U)=lim_j nu_E(u_j)=nu(d,E). This argument is repeated for each E and does not require a single point working for uncountably many divisors.

record.location: Proof, paragraph beginning 'Apply the valuative multiplier-ideal criterion'
record.detail: Equality of every divisorial Lelong number between U and d remains equality after each positive integral scaling. The valuative multiplier-ideal criterion then gives I(mU)=I(mphi) for every m>=1, hence [U]_I=d. Therefore U itself is a competitor and dominates every competitor by construction. Since the competitor family is defined solely from d, its largest member is independent of the chosen representative and is exactly the I-envelope P_theta[phi]_I; applying the same construction again is idempotent.

record.location: Proof, end of first-assertion argument: normalization and uniqueness
record.detail: Because U<=0, sup_X U<=0. If the supremum were negative, adding a sufficiently small positive constant would preserve theta-psh status and every multiplier ideal while retaining the inequality <=0, producing a strictly larger competitor; hence sup_X U=0. A normalized I-model in d is, by the I-model fixed-point definition, the largest element of this same competitor family, so it equals U. This proves existence, normalization, and uniqueness without a mass condition.

record.location: Proof, generalized Cantor construction through the zero-capacity conclusion
record.detail: With ell_0=1 and ell_m=exp(-4^m), the child-fitting inequalities 2 ell_1<ell_0 and 2 ell_{m+1}/ell_m=2 exp(-3*4^m)<1 hold, so two children of the prescribed next length fit at every stage. Assigning mass 2^-m to each stage-m interval gives a consistent limiting probability measure. Any singleton lies in nested stage intervals whose masses tend to zero, so the measure is nonatomic. The capacity series has terms 2^-m log(1/ell_m)=2^m for m>=1 and diverges; the cited generalized-Cantor criterion therefore makes the compact support F logarithmic-capacity zero, hence polar and pluripolar on P^1. Rescaling the initial circumference changes no convergence conclusion.

record.location: Proof, paragraph defining G_p, G_mu, and phi_s
record.detail: For normalized Fubini--Study area one, the normalized Green potential G_p exists with omega+dd^c G_p=delta_p and sup G_p=0. Integrating this kernel against the probability measure mu is legitimate as an extended psh construction. At any point outside the compact support F, positive distance from F bounds the kernel uniformly below, while normalization bounds it above, so G_mu is not identically minus infinity. Linearity/Fubini in currents gives omega+dd^c G_mu=mu. Thus phi_s=sG_mu is omega-psh for 0<=s<=1 and omega+dd^c phi_s=(1-s)omega+s mu.

record.location: Proof, paragraph on Lelong numbers and scaled multiplier ideals
record.detail: On a smooth Riemann surface the Lelong number of a positive (1,1)-current at a point equals its atomic mass there. Both omega and the constructed mu are nonatomic, so every point Lelong number of phi_s is zero. Prime divisors over a smooth curve give only point divisorial valuations; hence every divisorial Lelong number also vanishes. After every integral scaling m the profile still vanishes, and the valuative membership criterion puts 1 in I(m phi_s), proving I(m phi_s)=O_X for all m>=1 and [phi_s]_I=[0]_I.

record.location: Proof, BEGZ degree-one calculation and equations for the nonpluripolar mass
record.detail: The measure mu is supported on F. On X\F the Green potential is locally bounded (indeed its kernel is smooth away from the support), so plurifine locality identifies the degree-one nonpluripolar product there with the ordinary current, namely (1-s)omega. Nonpluripolar products put no mass on the pluripolar set F, and the smooth measure omega also gives F zero mass. Consequently the product is globally (1-s)omega and its total mass is 1-s.

results.theorem:
Let $U$ be an open subset of $\mathbb{C}^{n}$. Let $(u^{l}_{j})_{l}$ be a sequence of psh functions on $U$ and $u_{j}$ a psh function on $U$ for $1\leq j\leq m$. Let $(T_{l})_{l}$ be a sequence of closed positive currents satisfying Condition $(*)$ and $T_{l}$ converges to a closed positive current $T$ on $U$ as $l\to\infty$. Assume that one of the following conditions is satisfied:


$(i)$ $u_{j}^{l}\geq u_{j}$ and $u_{j}^{l}$ converges to $u_{j}$ in $L^{1}_{loc}$ as $l\to\infty$.


$(ii)$ $u_{j}^{l}$ increases to $u_{j}$ as $l\to\infty$ almost everywhere and $T$ has no mass on pluripolar sets.


Then, for every smooth weakly positive form $\Phi$ with compact support in $U$, we have



$\liminf_{l\to\infty}\int_{U}\langle\wedge_{j=1}^{m}dd^{c}u_{j}^{l}\dot{\wedge}T_{l}\rangle\wedge\Phi\geq\int_{U}\langle\wedge_{j=1}^{m}dd^{c}u_{j}\dot{\wedge}T\rangle\wedge\Phi.$

results.title: Polynomials associated to non-convex bodies
results.theorem:
Let $\{\psi_{n}\}$ be a locally uniformly bounded above family of plurisubharmonic functions on $\mathbb{C}^{d}$. Suppose for any subsequence $J$ of positive integers we have



$\bigl{(}\limsup_{n\in J}\psi_{n}(z)\bigr{)}^{*}=V(z)$



for all $z\in\mathbb{C}^{d}$ where $V\in PSH(\mathbb{C}^{d})\cap L^{\infty}_{loc}(\mathbb{C}^{d})$. Then $\psi_{n}\to V$ in $L_{loc}^{1}(\mathbb{C}^{d})$.

results.title: Viscosity solutions to quaternionic Monge-Ampère equations
results.theorem:
(1) (Theorem 3.1 in [22]) Let $v^{1},\ldots,v^{n}\in PSH\cap L_{loc}^{\infty}(\Omega)$. Let $\{v_{j}^{1}\}_{j\in\mathbb{N}},\ldots,\{v_{j}^{n}\}_{j\in\mathbb{N}}$ be decreasing sequences of $PSH$ functions in $\Omega$ such that $\lim_{j\rightarrow\infty}v_{j}^{t}=v^{t}$ pointwisely in $\Omega$ for each $t$. Then the currents $\triangle v_{j}^{1}\wedge\ldots\wedge\triangle v_{j}^{n}$ converge weakly to $\triangle v^{1}\wedge\ldots\wedge\triangle v^{n}$ as $j\rightarrow\infty$.
(2) (Proposition 4.1 in [23]) Let $\{u_{j}\}_{j\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence in $PSH\cap L_{loc}^{\infty}(\Omega)$ that increases to $u\in PSH\cap L_{loc}^{\infty}(\Omega)$ almost everywhere in $\Omega$ $($with respect to Lebesgue measure$)$. Then the currents $(\triangle u_{j})^{n}$ converge weakly to $(\triangle u)^{n}$ as $j\rightarrow\infty$.

results.title: Potts models on hierarchical lattices and Renormalization Group dynamics
results.theorem: Let $u_{j}$ be a sequence of plurisubharmonic functions on a domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{C}^{n}$. Assume that for all compacts $K\subset\Omega$ the sequence is dominated by a psh function. Then either $u_{j}\to-\infty$ on all compact subsets of $\Omega$ or there exists a subsequence $u_{j_{k}}$ which converges in $L^{1}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ to a psh function.

results.title: Kähler-Einstein metrics on families of Fano varieties
results.theorem:
Let $\Omega$ be a domain in $\mathbb{C}^{n}$.
If (uk)k∈ℕ∈PSH(Ω)ℕ(u_{k})_{k\in\mathbb{N}}\in\operatorname{PSH}(\Omega)^{\mathbb{N}} converges to a psh function $u$ in $L^{1}_{\mathrm{\ell oc}}(\Omega)$, then for any sequence $(x_{k})_{k}$ converges to $x\in\Omega$,



$u(x)\geq\limsup_{k\to+\infty}u_{k}(x_{k}).$

results.title: Weak convergence of Monge-Ampère measures on compact Hermitian manifolds
results.theorem: Let $\{u_{j}\}$ be a uniformly bounded sequence of $\omega$-psh functions. Assume $(\omega+dd^{c}u_{j})^{n}\leq C(\omega+dd^{c}\varphi_{j})^{n}$ for some uniformly bounded sequence $\{\varphi_{j}\}$ such that $\varphi_{j}\to\varphi\in PSH(X,\omega)$ in capacity. If $u_{j}\to u\in PSH(X,\omega)\cap L^{\infty}(X)$ in $L^{1}(X)$, then a subsequence of $(\omega+dd^{c}u_{j})^{n}$ converges weakly to $(\omega+dd^{c}u)^{n}$.

results.title: On the height of the universal abelian variety
results.theorem:
Let $(\varphi_{n})_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of plurisubharmonic functions that converges monotonically almost everywhere to a plurisubharmonic
function $\varphi$. Then, the sequence $(\varphi_{n})_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ converges in capacity to $\varphi$. See [GZ17, Proposition 4.25].

results.title: Super-potentials of positive closed currents, intersection theory and dynamics
results.theorem:
Let $(\varphi_{n})$ be a decreasing sequence of quasi-psh functions with
$dd^{c}\varphi_{n}\geq-\omega$. Then, either $\varphi_{n}$ converge
uniformly to $-\infty$ or $\varphi_{n}$ converge pointwise and also in
$\mathscr{L}^{p}$, $1\leq p<\infty$, to a quasi-psh function $\varphi$ with
$dd^{c}\varphi\geq-\omega$. Moreover, for every quasi-psh function
$\varphi$ with $dd^{c}\varphi\geq-\omega$, there is a
sequence $(\varphi_{n})$ of smooth functions such that
$dd^{c}\varphi_{n}\geq-\omega$ which decreases to $\varphi$.

results.title: Equidistribution for Random Polynomials and Systems of Random Holomorphic Sections
results.theorem:
Given a sequence $\{v_{n}\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ of subharmonic functions on a domain $G\subset\mathbb{R}^{m},\,\,m\geq 2$, which are locally uniformly bounded above on $G$, and a continuous and subharmonic function $v$ on $G$, assume that the following two conditions hold


(i)

$[\limsup_{n\rightarrow\infty}{v_{n}(z)}]^{*}\leq v(z)$ for all $z\in G$.



(ii)

There is a countable dense set $\{z_{s}\}$ in $G$ such that



$\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}{v_{n}(z_{s})}=v(z_{s}),\,\,s=1,2,\ldots.$






Then $v_{n}\rightarrow v$ in $L^{1}_{loc}(\mathbb{C}^{m})$.

results.title: Differentiability of the arithmetic volume function along the base conditions
results.theorem:
Let $\mathscr{X}$ be a normal, projective, and arithmetic variety, let $\mathscr{Y}$ be a reduced closed subscheme of $\mathscr{X}$, and let $\overline{\mathscr{D}}\coloneqq\left(\mathscr{D},g^{\overline{\mathscr{D}}}\right)$ be an arithmetic Cartier divisor on $\mathscr{X}$, and let $\bm{\mathscr{E}}=\left(\mathscr{E}_{1},\dots,\mathscr{E}_{l}\right)$ be a family of effective Cartier divisors on $\mathscr{X}$.
There then exist another $\mathscr{D}$-Green function $g^{\overline{\mathscr{D}}^{\prime}}$ and an $\mathscr{E}_{i}$-Green function $g^{\overline{\mathscr{E}}_{i}^{\prime}}$ on $\mathscr{X}_{\infty}^{\rm an}$ for each $i$ such that



$\mathop{\mathrm{Image}}\nolimits\left(\widehat{\Gamma}^{\rm s}\left(p\overline{\mathscr{D}};\bm{q}\cdot\boldsymbol{\mathscr{E}}\right)\to H^{0}\left(\left.\mathcal{O}_{\mathscr{X}}\left(p\mathscr{D}-\bm{q}\cdot\boldsymbol{\mathscr{E}}\right)\right|_{\mathscr{Y}}\right)\right)\subset\widehat{\Gamma}^{\rm s}\left(\left.\mathcal{O}_{\mathscr{X}}\left(p\overline{\mathscr{D}}^{\prime}-\bm{q}\cdot\overline{\boldsymbol{\mathscr{E}}}^{\prime}\right)\right|_{\mathscr{Y}}\right)$



for every $(p,\bm{q})\in(\mathbb{Z}_{\geqslant 0})^{l+1}$, where $\overline{\mathscr{D}}^{\prime}\coloneqq\left(\mathscr{D},g^{\overline{\mathscr{D}}^{\prime}}\right)$ and $\overline{\boldsymbol{\mathscr{E}}}^{\prime}\coloneqq\left(\left(\mathscr{E}_{1},g^{\overline{\mathscr{E}}_{1}^{\prime}}\right),\dots,\left(\mathscr{E}_{l},g^{\overline{\mathscr{E}}_{l}^{\prime}}\right)\right)$.

results.title: On the geometry of thin exceptional sets in Manin's Conjecture
results.theorem:
Let $X$ be a geometrically uniruled smooth projective variety of dimension $n$ defined over a number field $F$ and let $L$ be a big and semiample $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor on $X$. Suppose that $\rho(X)=\rho(\overline{X})$ and $a(X,L)L+K_{X}$ is rigid. As we vary over all geometrically integral subvarieties $Y\subset X$ defined over $F$ such that either $L|_{Y}$ is not big or



$(a(Y,L|_{Y}),b(F,Y,L|_{Y}))\geq(a(X,L),b(F,X,L))$



in the lexicographic order, the points



$\bigcup_{Y}Y(F)$



are contained in a thin subset of $X(F)$.

results.theorem:
Let $X$ be a projective variety of dimension $n$ defined over a number field $k$. Let $S$ be a finite set of places of $k$. For each $v\in S$, let $D_{0,v},\ldots,D_{n,v}$ be effective Cartier divisors on $X$, defined over $k$, in general position. Let $A$ be an ample Cartier divisor on $X$ and let $c_{i,v}$ be rational numbers such that $A-c_{i,v}D_{i,v}$ is a nef $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor for all $i$ and for all $v\in S$. Let $\epsilon>0$. Then there exists a proper Zariski-closed subset $Z\subset X$ such that for all points $P\in X(k)\setminus Z$,



$\sum_{v\in S}\sum_{i=0}^{n}c_{i,v}\lambda_{D_{i,v},v}(P)<(n+1+\epsilon)h_{A}(P).$

Let ${\mathcal{Y}}$ be an irreducible scheme of finite type over ${\rm Spec\,}\mathbb{Z}$, together with a morphism $f:{\mathcal{Y}}\rightarrow{\mathcal{X}}$. Let $U$ be an open dense subscheme of ${\mathcal{Y}}$. Then for all $\sigma$ in a density $1$ subset of $\bigcup_{n>0}H^{0}_{Ar}({\mathcal{X}},{\overline{\mathcal{L}}}^{\otimes n})$, we have the equivalence



$\mathrm{div}(f^{*}\sigma)_{horiz}\,\textup{is irreducible}\Leftrightarrow(\mathrm{div}(f^{*}\sigma)\cap U)_{horiz}\,\textup{is irreducible}.$

results.title: On the arithmetic case of Vojta's conjecture with truncated counting functions
results.theorem:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety over $\mathbb{Q}$ and let $D_{1},...,D_{m}$ be different prime divisors on $X$ defined over $\mathbb{Q}$. Suppose that $D_{1},...,D_{m}$ are linearly dependent modulo linear equivalence over $\mathbb{Q}$. Let $P\in X(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ be an algebraic point not in the support of $D=D_{1}+...+D_{m}$. There is a proper Zariski closed subset $Z\subseteq X$ such that for every given $\epsilon>0$ and each place $v\in M_{\mathbb{Q}}$, the following inequality holds for all $x\in X(\mathbb{Q})$ not in $Z$:


(1.4)

$\lambda_{X,v}(P,x)<(\log^{*}h_{X}(\mathscr{O}(D),x))\exp\left(\frac{(1+\epsilon)N^{(1)}_{X}}{\log^{*}N^{(1)}_{X}}\log^{*}_{2}N^{(1)}_{X}+O(1)\right)$



where the bounded error term $O(1)$ does not depend on $x$, and $N^{(1)}_{X}=N_{X}^{(1)}(D,x)$.

results.title: On equivalent conjectures for minimal log discrepancies on smooth threefolds
results.theorem:
Let $P\in X$ be the germ of a smooth threefold and $\mathfrak{m}$ be the maximal ideal in $\mathscr{O}_{X}$ defining $P$. Fix a positive rational number $q$. Let $\mathscr{P}$ be a property of canonical pairs $(X,\mathfrak{a}^{q})$ for ideals $\mathfrak{a}$ on $X$. Then the following statements are equivalent.


(i)

Fix a non-negative rational number $s$. Then there exists a positive integer $l$ depending only on $q$ and $s$ such that if $\mathfrak{a}$ is an ideal on $X$ satisfying that $(X,\mathfrak{a}^{q})$ is canonical and has the property $\mathscr{P}$, then there exists a divisor $E$ over $X$ which computes $\operatorname{mld}_{P}(X,\mathfrak{a}^{q}\mathfrak{m}^{s})$ and satisfies the inequality $a_{E}(X)\leq l$.



(ii)

Fix a non-negative rational number $s$ and a positive integer $b$. Then there exists a positive integer $l$ depending only on $q$, $s$ and $b$ such that if $\mathfrak{a}$ and $\mathfrak{b}$ are ideals on $X$ satisfying that $(X,\mathfrak{a}^{q})$ is canonical and has the property $\mathscr{P}$ and that $\mathfrak{b}$ contains $\mathfrak{m}^{b}$, then there exists a divisor $E$ over $X$ which computes $\operatorname{mld}_{P}(X,\mathfrak{a}^{q}\mathfrak{b}^{s})$ and satisfies the inequality $a_{E}(X)\leq l$.

results.title: Sufficient conditions for the dirichlet property
results.theorem:
Let $X$ be an integral projective scheme over $\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $(D,g)$ be an adelic $\mathbb{R}$-Cartier divisor on $X$. For any s∈Rat(X)×s\in\operatorname{Rat}(X)^{\times}, we have the following:



$\begin{cases}\lambda_{\max}(D,g)=\lambda_{\max}(D+(s),g-\log|s|),\\
\lambda_{\max}^{\mathrm{asy}}(D,g)=\lambda_{\max}^{\mathrm{asy}}(D+(s),g-\log|s|),\\
\hat{\mu}_{\mathrm{ess}}(D,g)=\hat{\mu}_{\mathrm{ess}}(D+(s),g-\log|s|).\end{cases}$

results.title: A note on multiplier ideal sheaves on complex spaces with singularities
results.theorem:
Let $X$ be a complex space of pure dimension $n$ and $\varphi\in L_{\text{loc}}^{1}(X_{\text{reg}})$ with respect to the Lebesgue measure. Let $X\hookrightarrow\Omega\subset\mathbb{C}^{n+r}$ be a local embedding such that $\mathscr{I}_{X}$ is generated by holomorphic functions $g_{1},\dots,g_{m}$ on $\Omega$.


The Nadel-Ohsawa multiplier ideal sheaf $\widehat{\mathscr{I}}(\varphi)$ on $X$ is defined to be the fractional ideal sheaf of germs of meromorphic functions $f\in\mathscr{M}_{X,x}$ such that $|f|^{2}e^{-2\varphi}$ is locally integrable at $x$ on $X$ with respect to the measure $dV_{X}[\Psi]$, where $\Psi=r\log(|g_{1}|^{2}+\cdots+|g_{m}|^{2})$. One can check that $\widehat{\mathscr{I}}(\varphi)$ is independent of the local embedding of $X$ and the choice of generators of $\mathscr{I}_{X}$.

results.title: MacPherson's Conjecture via Hörmander Estimate
results.theorem:
Let $X$ be a complex analytic space of pure dimension $n$ and $ds^{2}$ be a hermitian metric on a dense Zariski open subset $X^{o}\subset X_{\rm reg}$ with $\omega$ its fundamental form. Let $\pi:M\to X$ be a proper holomorphic map such that $M$ is smooth and $\pi:\pi^{-1}X^{o}\to X^{o}$ is biholomorphic. Let $(L,h)$ be a holomorphic line bundle with a (possibly) singular hermitian metric $h$ on $M$. Denote by $\mathscr{I}(h)$ the associated multiplier ideal sheaf. Assume that for every point $x\in X$, there is a neighborhood $x\in U$, a Kähler metric $g_{U}$ on $U\cap X^{o}$, a (possibly) singular hermitian metric $h^{\prime}\sim h$ on $L|_{\pi^{-1}U}$ and a bounded $C^{\infty}$ strictly plurisubharmonic function $\Phi$ on $U\cap X^{o}$ such that



$g_{U}\sim\omega|_{U\cap X^{o}}\lesssim\sqrt{-1}\partial\bar{\partial}\Phi$



on $U$ and



$\displaystyle\sqrt{-1}\Theta_{h^{\prime}}(L)\geq C\omega$



on $\pi^{-1}(U)$ as currents for some $C\in\mathbb{R}$.
Then the complex of sheaves



$\displaystyle 0\to\pi_{\ast}(K_{M}\otimes L\otimes\mathscr{I}(h))\to\mathscr{D}^{n,0}_{X,ds^{2}}(L,h)\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\bar{\partial}}}{{\to}}\mathscr{D}^{n,1}_{X,ds^{2}}(L,h)\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\bar{\partial}}}{{\to}}\cdots\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\bar{\partial}}}{{\to}}\mathscr{D}^{n,n}_{X,ds^{2}}(L,h)\to 0$



is exact. Here $\mathscr{D}^{n,\bullet}_{X,ds^{2}}(L,h)$ denotes the complex consisting of measurable $L|_{X^{o}}$-valued $(n,\bullet)$-forms $\alpha$ such that $\alpha$ and its distributive $\bar{\partial}\alpha$ are locally square integrable.

results.title: A non-Archimedean Ohsawa-Takegoshi extension theorem
results.theorem:
Let $\varphi$ be a quasisubharmonic function on $X$ with $\varphi\leq 0$.
For any $x\in X$, the local multiplier ideal of $\varphi$ at $x$, denoted $\mathcal{J}(\varphi)_{x}$, consists of those germs $f\in\mathcal{O}_{X,x}$ such that for all $\epsilon>0$, there is an affinoid neighborhood $V_{\epsilon}$ of $x$ on which $f$ is defined such that



$\sup_{V_{\epsilon}\backslash Z(\varphi)}|f|e^{-(1+\epsilon)\varphi-A}<+\infty.$

results.title: Kähler-Einstein metrics on stable varieties and log canonical pairs
results.theorem:
Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$, $dV$ some volume form, $D=\sum a_{i}D_{i}$ a $\mathbb{R}$-divisor with coefficients in $(-\infty,1]$ and defining sections $s_{i}$, $E=\sum c_{\alpha}E_{\alpha}$ an effective $\mathbb{R}$-divisor such that $D_{red}+E$ has snc support, and $\theta$ a semipositive form with $\int_{X}\theta^{n}>0$ such that $\{\theta\}-c_{1}(E)$ is a Kähler class. Then the $\theta$-psh function $\varphi$ with full Monge-Ampère mass, which is a solution of



$\langle(\theta+dd^{c}\phi)^{n}\rangle=\frac{e^{\varphi}dV}{\prod_{i}|s_{i}|^{2a_{j}}}$



is smooth outside of $\mathrm{Supp}(D)\cup\mathrm{Supp}(E)$.

results.title: On the behavior of adjoint ideals under pure morphisms
results.theorem:
Let $f:Y\to X$ be a faithfully flat morphism between normal complex varieties.
Let $D$ be a reduced divisor and $\Gamma$ be an effective $\mathbb{Q}$-Weil divisor on $X$ such that $D$ and $\Gamma$ have no common components.
Suppose that the flat pullback $E:=f^{*}D$ of $D$ under $f$ is a reduced divisor on $Y$ and the $\mathcal{O}_{X}$-algebra $\bigoplus_{i\geqslant 0}\mathcal{O}_{X}(\lfloor-i(K_{X}+D+\Gamma)\rfloor)$ is finitely generated.
For any coherent ideal sheaf $\mathfrak{a}\subseteq\mathcal{O}_{X}$ whose zero locus contains no components of $D$
and for any real number $t>0$, one has



$\mathrm{adj}_{E}(Y,E+f^{*}\Gamma,(\mathfrak{a}\mathcal{O}_{Y})^{t})\subseteq\mathrm{adj}_{D}(X,D+\Gamma,\mathfrak{a}^{t})\mathcal{O}_{Y}.$

results.title: On the behavior of adjoint ideals under pure morphisms
results.theorem:
Let $f:Y\to X$ be a pure morphism between normal complex varieties, $D$ be a reduced divisor
and $\Gamma$ be an effective $\mathbb{Q}$-Weil divisor on $X$ that has no common components with $D$.
Suppose that $K_{X}+D+\Gamma$ is $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier and the cycle-theoretic pullback $E:=f^{\natural}D$ of $D$ under $f$ is a disjoint union of prime divisors on $Y$.
For any coherent ideal sheaf $\mathfrak{a}\subseteq\mathcal{O}_{X}$ whose zero locus contains no components of $D$ and for any real number $t>0$, one has



$f_{*}\mathrm{adj}_{E}(Y,E+f^{*}\Gamma,(\mathfrak{a}\mathcal{O}_{Y})^{t})\cap\mathcal{O}_{X}\subseteq\mathrm{adj}_{D}(X,D+\Gamma,\mathfrak{a}^{t}).$

results.title: On the number of $p$-hypergeometric solutions of KZ equations
results.theorem:
Suppose $M$ is compact and $\omega$ is a meromorphic multivalued
$r$-form on $M$ with only finitely many determinations and whose polar set is
contained in an arrangement-like hypersurface $D$. Then the following properties are equivalent:


(i)

the form $\omega$ is square integrable in the sense that
$\int_{M}\omega\wedge\bar{\omega}$ converges;



(ii)

the form $\omega$ has positive logarithmic order along any dense stratum of $D$;



(iii)

if $\tilde{M}\to M$ is a proper surjective map with $\tilde{M}$ a complex manifold
of the same dimension as $M$ and such that $\omega$ becomes a univalued
$d$-form on $\tilde{M}$, then the latter form is regular.

results.title: On the non-archimedean Monge-Ampère equation in mixed characteristic
results.theorem:
Let $n\in{\mathbb{N}}$ such that resolution of singularities and embedded resolution of singularities hold in dimension $n+1$ over $R$.
Let $X$ be a regular projective variety over $K$ of dimension $n$ and let $\theta$ be a closed $(1,1)$-form on ${X^{\mathrm{an}}}$ with ample de Rham class $\{\theta\}$.
We assume that the subadditivity conjecture 4.1 holds for all projective regular models of $X$.
We consider a positive Radon measure $\mu$ on $X^{\rm an}$ of total mass $\{\theta\}^{n}$ which is supported on the skeleton of a projective SNC-model of $X$.
Then there is a continuous $\theta$-psh function $\varphi$ on ${X^{\mathrm{an}}}$ such that ${\rm MA}_{\theta}(\varphi)=\mu$ and $\varphi$ is unique up to additive constants.

results.title: Degenerate complex Monge-Ampère equations over compact Kähler manifolds
results.theorem:
Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension $n$ and let $\chi$ be a $(1,1)$-cohomology class admitting a smooth closed semipositive $(1,1)$-form $\omega$ such that $\int_{X}\omega^{n}>0$.


(A) For any $L\log^{n+\varepsilon}L$-density $v\geq 0$, $\varepsilon>0$ such that $\int_{X}v=\int_{X}\chi^{n}$, there exists a unique closed positive current $T\in\operatorname{BT}_{\chi}$ such that $T^{n}=v$. Moreover, this current possesses bounded local potentials over $X$ and continuous local potentials outside a complex analytic set $\Sigma_{\chi}\subset X$. This set depends only on the class $\chi$ and can be taken to be empty if the class $\chi$ is Kähler.


(B)
In the special case of a density $v\geq 0$ possessing complex analytic singularities the current $T$ is also smooth outside the complex analytic subset $\Sigma_{\chi}\cup Z(v)\subset X$, where $Z(v)$ is the set of zeros and poles of $v$.

results.title: Kähler-Einstein metrics on stable varieties and log canonical pairs
results.theorem:
Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$, $dV$ some volume form, $D=\sum a_{i}D_{i}$ a $\mathbb{R}$-divisor with coefficients in $(-\infty,1]$ and defining sections $s_{i}$, $E=\sum c_{\alpha}E_{\alpha}$ an effective $\mathbb{R}$-divisor such that $D_{red}+E$ has snc support, and $\theta$ a semipositive form with $\int_{X}\theta^{n}>0$ such that $\{\theta\}-c_{1}(E)$ is a Kähler class. Then the $\theta$-psh function $\varphi$ with full Monge-Ampère mass, which is a solution of



$\langle(\theta+dd^{c}\phi)^{n}\rangle=\frac{e^{\varphi}dV}{\prod_{i}|s_{i}|^{2a_{j}}}$



is smooth outside of $\mathrm{Supp}(D)\cup\mathrm{Supp}(E)$.

results.title: Riemannian geometry of Kahler-Einstein currents III: compactness of Kahler-Einstein manifolds of negative scalar curvature
results.theorem:
Let $\pi:\mathcal{X}\rightarrow\mathcal{S}$ be a stable family of $n$-dimensional canonical models over a projective normal variety $\mathcal{S}$. Let $\omega_{t}$ be the unique Kähler-Einstein metric on $\mathcal{X}_{t}$ for $t\in\mathcal{S}^{\circ}$ and $h$ be the hermitian metric on the relative canonical sheaf $K_{\mathcal{X}^{\circ}/\mathcal{S}^{\circ}}$ defined by



$h_{t}=(\omega_{t}^{n})^{-1}.$



The curvature $\theta=\sqrt{-1}\partial\overline{\partial}\log h$ of $(K_{\mathcal{X}^{\circ}/\mathcal{S}^{\circ}},h)$ extends uniquely to a closed nonnegative $(1,1)$-current on $\mathcal{X}$ with vanishing Lelong number everywhere. Furthermore,




(1)

$\theta|_{\mathcal{X}_{t}}=\omega_{t}$ for $t\in\mathcal{S}^{\circ}$.



(2)

$\theta|_{\mathcal{X}_{t}}$ is the unique canonical Kähler-Einstein current on the semi-log canonical model $\mathcal{X}_{t}$ for any $t\in\mathcal{S}\setminus\mathcal{S}^{\circ}$.



(3)

$K_{\mathcal{X}/\mathcal{S}}$ is nef on $\mathcal{X}$.



Moreover, if all the fibres of $\pi:\mathcal{X}\rightarrow\mathcal{S}$ have at worst log terminal singularities, then $\theta$ has bounded local potentials on $\mathcal{X}$.

for some $1\leq i_{1},\ldots,i_{r}\leq d$.



Furthermore, locally near $a$ we can express



$(f\circ\pi)=\varepsilon\cdot\prod_{k=1}^{r}y_{i_{k}}^{N_{i_{k}}}\quad\text{and}\quad\pi^{*}\left(\bigwedge_{i=1}^{d}{\mathrm{d}}x_{i}\right)=\eta\cdot\prod_{k=1}^{r}y_{i_{k}}^{\nu_{i_{k}}-1}\cdot\bigwedge_{i=1}^{d}{\mathrm{d}}y_{i},$



for some $1\leq i_{1},\ldots,i_{r}\leq d$ and $\varepsilon,\eta$ real analytic functions with $\varepsilon(0),\eta(0)\neq 0$. See e.g. [Igu00, Ch. 3 and 11] for more details.

results.title: A Kümmer construction for Chern-Ricci flat balanced manifolds
results.theorem:
Let $(\tilde{M},\tilde{\omega})$ be an $n$-dimensional non-Kähler Calabi-Yau compact orbifold with isolated singularities, endowed with $\tilde{\omega}$ a singular Chern-Ricci flat balanced metric, and let $M$ be a crepant resolution of $\tilde{M}$. Suppose that the operator $\Delta_{\omega}+|\partial\omega|_{\omega}^{2}Id$ has vanishing kernel on $\tilde{M}$. Then $M$ admits a Chern-Ricci flat balanced metric such that



$[\omega^{n-1}]=[\hat{\omega}^{n-1}]=[\tilde{\omega}^{n-1}]+(-1)^{n-1}\varepsilon^{(2n-2)}(\sum_{i=1}^{k_{j}}\sum_{j=1}^{k}a_{j}^{i}PD[E_{j}^{i}])^{n-1},$



where $PD[E_{j}^{i}]$ denotes the Poincaré dual of the class $[E_{j}^{i}]$, represented by the $i$-th component of the $j$-th exceptional divisor arising from the resolution of the corresponding singularity.

results.title: Extremal Kähler Poincaré type metrics on toric varieties
results.theorem:
Let $Z\subset X$ be a simple normal crossing divisor in a compact complex $n$-dimensional Kähler manifold $(X,\omega_{0})$.
A Kähler metric $\omega$ on $X\setminus Z$ is said to be of Poincaré type of class $[\omega_{0}]$ if


$\bullet$

On any open subset $U\subset X$ with holomorphic coordinates $(z_{1},\ldots,z_{n})$ such that $Z\cap U$ is given by $z_{1}\cdots z_{k}=0$,
$\omega$ is quasi-isometric to the $(1,1)$-form



$\omega_{\rm mod}=\sqrt{-1}\Big{(}\sum_{j=1}^{k}\frac{1}{|z_{j}|^{2}(\log|z_{j}|)^{2}}dz_{j}\wedge d\bar{z}_{j}+\sum_{j=k+1}^{n}dz_{j}\wedge d\bar{z}_{j}\Big{)}$



near $Z$, and



$\bullet$

$\omega=\omega_{0}+dd^{c}\varphi$ where $\varphi$ is a smooth function on $X\setminus Z$
and $\varphi=O\big{(}\sum_{j=1}^{k}\log(-\log|z_{j}|)\big{)}$ in the coordinates $(z_{1},\ldots,z_{n})$ as above,
with $d\varphi$ having bounded derivatives of any order with respect to the model metric $\omega_{\rm mod}$ above.

results.title: On Skoda's theorem for Nadel-Lebesgue multiplier ideal sheaves on singular complex spaces and regularity of weak Kähler-Einstein metrics
results.theorem:
$(1)$ Let $\pi:\widetilde{X}\to X$ be a log resolution of the Jacobian ideal $\mathcal{J}ac_{X}$ of $X$ and $\widehat{K}_{\widetilde{X}/X}$ be the Mather discrepancy divisor. Then, we have the image



$\emph{Im}\left(\pi^{*}\Omega_{X}^{n}\hookrightarrow\Omega_{\widetilde{X}}^{n}\right)=\mathcal{O}_{\widetilde{X}}(-\widehat{K}_{\widetilde{X}/X})\cdot\Omega_{\widetilde{X}}^{n},$



and



$\mathscr{I}_{\emph{NL}}(\varphi)=\pi_{*}\left(\mathcal{O}_{\widetilde{X}}(\widehat{K}_{\widetilde{X}/X})\otimes\mathscr{I}(\varphi\circ\pi)\right).$



Furthermore, we can deduce that $\mathscr{I}_{\emph{NL}}(\varphi+\log|\mathcal{J}ac_{X}|)=\mathscr{I}_{\emph{NO}}(\varphi)$, the Nadel-Ohsawa multiplier ideal sheaf associated to $\varphi$ on $X$.


$(2)$ When $X$ is normal and $\varphi$ has analytic singularities, $\mathscr{I}_{\emph{NL}}(\varphi)$ coincides with the Mather multiplier ideal sheaf defined in [9].


$(3)$ For any $\varphi\in\emph{QPsh}(X)$, it follows that $\mathscr{I}_{\emph{NL}}(\varphi)\subset\mathscr{M}_{X}$ is a coherent fractional ideal sheaf and satisfies the strong openness, i.e., $\mathscr{I}_{\emph{NL}}(\varphi)=\bigcup\limits_{\varepsilon>0}\mathscr{I}_{\emph{NL}}\big{(}(1+\varepsilon)\varphi\big{)}$.

results.title: Zeta functions and Bernstein-Sato polynomials for ideals in dimension two
results.theorem:
Let $\mathcal{I}$ be an ideal of $\mathbf{C}[x]=\mathbf{C}[x_{1},\ldots,x_{n}]$, with $0=(0,\ldots,0)\in\operatorname{supp}\mathcal{I}$, and $g$ a nonzero polynomial in $\mathbf{C}[x]$. In $\mathbf{A}^{n}(\mathbf{C})$ we consider the support of $\mathcal{I}$ and the volume form $gdx=gdx_{1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dx_{n}$. By an embedded resolution of $(\mathcal{I},gdx)$, we mean in this paper a composition



$h=h_{1}\circ\cdots\circ h_{t}:Y=Y_{t}\to Y_{0}=\mathbf{A}^{n}(\mathbf{C})$



of blowing-ups $h_{i}:Y_{i}\to Y_{i-1}$ in smooth centra $C_{i-1}\subseteq Y_{i-1}$, such that


(i)

$h$ is a principalization of $\mathcal{I}$; i.e.,


(a)

for all $i\in\{1,\ldots,t\}$, the exceptional divisor of the morphism $h_{1}\circ\cdots\circ h_{i}:Y_{i}\to Y_{0}$ is a simple normal crossings divisor on $Y_{i}$, having moreover simple normal crossings with $C_{i}$ for $i\in\{1,\ldots,t-1\}$, and



(b)

the total transform (pull-back) $h^{\ast}(\mathcal{I})$ of $\mathcal{I}$ is the ideal of a simple normal crossings divisor $F$ on $Y$;






(ii)

$h$ is an embedded resolution of singularities of the locus $g^{-1}(0)\subseteq\mathbf{A}^{n}(\mathbf{C})$, where we denote by $G=\operatorname{div}g\circ h$ the (principal) simple normal crossings divisor on $Y$ associated to $g\circ h$; and



(iii)

$F+G$ is (still) a simple normal crossings divisor on $Y$.

100: \subsection{Four comparisons, and why there are four}
101: \label{sec:ch51-four}
102: 
103: Let \(\varphi\) and \(\psi\) be quasi-psh functions on \(X\).  Four
104: relations between them occur in this book, and each is used somewhere in
105: \cref{part:complex,part:comparisons}:
106: \begin{enumerate}
107: \item pointwise order, \(\varphi\leq\psi\);
108: \item ordinary singularity type, \(\varphi\preceq\psi\), meaning
109:       \(\varphi\leq\psi+O(1)\);
110: \item \(P\)-comparison, \(\varphi\preceq_P\psi\), meaning
111:       \(P_\theta[\varphi]\leq P_\theta[\psi]\);
112: \item \(\mathcal I\)-comparison, \(\varphi\preceq_{\mathcal I}\psi\),
113:       meaning \(\mathcal I(m\varphi)\subseteq\mathcal I(m\psi)\) for every
114:       \(m\geq1\).
115: \end{enumerate}
116: Each is coarser than the one before it, and the induced equivalence
117: relations \(=\), \(\sim\), \(\sim_P\), \(\sim_{\mathcal I}\) are
118: correspondingly coarser.  The four are genuinely distinct.  Bounded
119: perturbations separate the first from the second.  The function
120: \(-\log(-\log|z|^2)\) of \Cref{ex:appH-loglog} separates the second from
121: the third: it is unbounded, hence not ordinarily equivalent to \(0\), but
122: its \(P\)-envelope is \(0\).  \Cref{ex:ch51-cantor} separates the third
123: from the fourth, by exhibiting a potential all of whose Lelong numbers
124: vanish --- so that it is \(\mathcal I\)-equivalent to \(0\) --- but whose
125: nonpluripolar mass is \(1/2\) while the mass of \(0\) is \(1\).  The
126: \(P\)-projection theorem then forbids \(P\)-equivalence.
127: 
128: There is a useful mnemonic.  The relation \(\sim\) remembers the
129: potential up to a bounded error; \(\sim_P\) remembers exactly the
130: data that nonpluripolar masses and relative energies can see; and
131: \(\sim_{\mathcal I}\) remembers exactly the data that divisorial
132: valuations can see.  The last of these is what analytification produces
133: (\Cref{chap:valuative-analytification}), and it is also the datum on which
134: the analytic trace of \Cref{chap:operations-trace} depends.  The target of
135: that operator is nevertheless a \(P\)-class: every trace is
136: \(\mathcal I\)-good, and two choices are \(P\)-equivalent.  This upgrade
137: from \(\mathcal I\)-data at the source to \(P\)-uniqueness at the target is
138: a theorem about restricted quasi-equisingular approximants, not a formal
139: property of the three quotients.

1698: \label{warn:ch51-so-scope}
1699: The theorem identifies two packages of information --- all multiplier
1700: ideals, and all divisorial Lelong numbers --- with each other.  It does

1705: such behaviour.  The whole difficulty of \Cref{sec:ch51-p-vs-i} is that
1706: the missing information is not only ``\(O(1)\)-sized'': it can change a
1707: nonpluripolar mass.

1677: \(\liminf_m m^{-1}\ord_E\mathcal I(m\varphi)\geq\nu(\varphi,E)\), which
1678: uses no approximation theorem, is to apply
1679: \Cref{prop:ch51-valuative-criterion} with \(\lambda=m\): every
1680: \(f\in\mathcal I(m\varphi)\) satisfies
1681: \(\ord_E(f)\geq m\nu(\varphi,E)-A(E)\), and \(A(E)\) does not depend on
1682: \(m\).
1683: 
1684: \emph{Item \cref{itm:ch51-so:equivalence}.}  We prove a cycle of
1685: implications.  Suppose \(\mathcal I(m\varphi)=\mathcal I(m\psi)\) for
1686: every integer \(m\geq1\).  Applying
1687: \eqref{eq:complex-lelong-from-ideals} to both sides gives
1688: \(\nu(\varphi,E)=\nu(\psi,E)\) for every prime divisor \(E\) over \(X\).
1689: Suppose next that all these divisorial numbers agree.  Then
1690: \Cref{prop:ch51-valuative-criterion} produces the same membership
1691: criterion for \(\mathcal I(\lambda\varphi)\) and
1692: \(\mathcal I(\lambda\psi)\) at every real \(\lambda>0\), so the two
1693: sheaves coincide.  Finally, equality at every real \(\lambda>0\)
1694: trivially implies equality at every integer \(m\geq1\).  This closes the
1695: cycle.
1696: 
1697: \begin{warning}{What item \cref{itm:ch51-so:equivalence} does not say}
1698: \label{warn:ch51-so-scope}
1699: The theorem identifies two packages of information --- all multiplier
1700: ideals, and all divisorial Lelong numbers --- with each other.  It does
1701: \emph{not} identify either of them with the ordinary singularity type.  A
1702: potential can have all divisorial Lelong numbers equal to zero and still
1703: be unbounded, as in \Cref{ex:ch51-disk-three-types} and, globally, in
1704: \Cref{ex:ch51-cantor}; log--log poles are the standard local source of
1705: such behaviour.  The whole difficulty of \Cref{sec:ch51-p-vs-i} is that
1706: the missing information is not only ``\(O(1)\)-sized'': it can change a
1707: nonpluripolar mass.
1708: \end{warning}

{"source_id":"p148_ch51_dependency_v4","source_sha256":"7f2b4890d6332d042113d89bfa921f0f58bbfcbd63c5a18a9eff21469a0fc40b","start_line":2116,"end_line":2315,"text":"2116: \subsection{Bidegree one}
2117: \label{sec:ch51-npp-bidegree-one}
2118: 
2119: In bidegree \((1,1)\) the nonpluripolar product has a completely explicit
2120: description, and every mass computation in this chapter uses it.
2121: 
2122: \begin{lemma}\label{lem:ch51-npp-bidegree-one}
2123: Let \(\varphi\in\PSH(X,\theta)\).  Then
2124: \[
2125:  \langle\theta_\varphi\rangle
2126:  =\one_{\{\varphi>-\infty\}}\,\theta_\varphi
2127: \]
2128: as measures on \(X\) when \(n=1\), and as currents in general.  In
2129: particular \(\langle\theta_\varphi\rangle\leq\theta_\varphi\), the two
2130: agree if and only if \(\theta_\varphi\) puts no mass on the pluripolar
2131: set \(\{\varphi=-\infty\}\), and, for \(n=1\),
2132: \[
2133:  M_\theta(\varphi)
2134:  =\int_X\theta_\varphi-\theta_\varphi(\{\varphi=-\infty\})
2135:  =\int_X\{\theta\}-\theta_\varphi(\{\varphi=-\infty\}).
2136: \]
2137: \end{lemma}
2138: 
2139: \begin{proof}
2140: Take \(p=1\) in \eqref{eq:complex-npp-truncation}.  With
2141: \(O_k=\{\varphi>-k\}\) and \(\varphi_k:=\max\{\varphi,-k\}\), plurifine
2142: locality gives
2143: \[
2144:  \one_{O_k}\theta_\varphi=\one_{O_k}\theta_{\varphi_k}
2145: \]
2146: for every \(k\), since \(\varphi=\varphi_k\) on \(O_k\).  The sets
2147: \(O_k\) increase to \(\{\varphi>-\infty\}\), so the increasing limit of
2148: the left-hand sides is \(\one_{\{\varphi>-\infty\}}\theta_\varphi\), while
2149: the increasing limit of the right-hand sides is by definition
2150: \(\langle\theta_\varphi\rangle\).  The inequality
2151: \(\langle\theta_\varphi\rangle\leq\theta_\varphi\) and the criterion for
2152: equality are immediate, and the mass formula for \(n=1\) follows because
2153: then \(\theta_\varphi\) is a positive measure of total mass
2154: \(\int_X\{\theta\}\), by Stokes.
2155: \end{proof}
2156: 
2157: \begin{remark}[The higher-degree analogue fails]
2158: \label{rem:ch51-npp-no-restriction}
2159: For \(p\geq2\) there is no formula
2160: \(\langle\theta_{\varphi_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge\theta_{\varphi_p}\rangle
2161: =\one_{\{\text{all }\varphi_j>-\infty\}}
2162: \theta_{\varphi_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge\theta_{\varphi_p}\), because the
2163: right-hand side has no meaning: the unrestricted product of unbounded
2164: potentials is not defined.  The nonpluripolar product is precisely the
2165: substitute, and \Cref{lem:ch51-npp-bidegree-one} is the one degree in
2166: which the substitute can be described by a restriction.  This is why the
2167: computations in \Cref{ex:ch51-cantor} take place on a curve and the
2168: computations in \Cref{ex:ch51-blowup-mass} on a surface use a Siu
2169: decomposition instead.
2170: \end{remark}
2171: 
2172: \subsection{The ledger}
2173: \label{sec:ch51-npp-ledger}
2174: 
2175: \begin{theorem}\label{thm:complex-npp-ledger}
2176: The product \eqref{eq:complex-global-npp} is a closed positive
2177: \((p,p)\)-current.  It is symmetric and multilinear in the currents,
2178: local for the plurifine topology, agrees with the Bedford--Taylor
2179: product for locally bounded potentials, and charges no pluripolar set.
2180: If \(\varphi_j\) is replaced by a less singular potential in the same
2181: class, every mixed total mass can only increase.  Proper bimeromorphic
2182: pullback preserves total masses.
2183: \end{theorem}
2184: 
2185: \begin{proof}[Why truncation is sufficient]
2186: Plurifine locality makes the truncations in
2187: \eqref{eq:complex-npp-truncation} compatible.  Their masses on relatively
2188: compact sets are uniformly controlled after wedging with a K\"ahler
2189: form, so the increasing limit is locally finite.  Bedford--Taylor
2190: integration by parts yields closedness and symmetry before passage to
2191: the limit.  Monotonicity is the global theorem of
2192: \cite{BEGZ10}; bimeromorphic invariance follows by pulling the
2193: truncations to the common isomorphism locus, since the omitted sets are
2194: pluripolar.
2195: \end{proof}
2196: 
2197: The argument deserves to be run through once more, slowly, because five
2198: distinct assertions are packed into the statement and they have five
2199: different proofs.
2200: 
2201: \emph{Closedness, symmetry, multilinearity.}  Each truncated product
2202: \(\bigwedge_j\ddc\max\{u_j,-k\}\) is a closed positive current, symmetric
2203: and multilinear in its arguments, by Bedford--Taylor theory
2204: \cite{BT76,BT82}.  These properties are stable under the increasing limit
2205: of the restrictions \(\one_{O_k}(\cdot)\): positivity and symmetry are
2206: pointwise, multilinearity holds at each level \(k\), and closedness
2207: passes to the limit because a limit of closed currents in the weak
2208: topology is closed.
2209: 
2210: \emph{Plurifine locality.}  If \(u_j=v_j\) on a plurifine open set \(O\)
2211: for every \(j\), then the truncations coincide on
2212: \(O\cap O_k\), hence so do the limits on \(O\).  This is the property that
2213: makes the whole construction work, and it is
2214: \cite{BT87}.
2215: 
2216: \emph{Agreement with Bedford--Taylor.}  If every \(u_j\) is locally
2217: bounded, then \(O_k\) is the whole set for \(k\) large, and the
2218: truncations stabilize.
2219: 
2220: \emph{No mass on pluripolar sets.}  Assume that the increasing limit in
2221: \eqref{eq:complex-npp-truncation} is locally finite.  In the compact K\"ahler
2222: situation of \eqref{eq:complex-global-npp}, this local finiteness follows from
2223: \cite[Proposition~1.6]{BEGZ10}.  Let \(A\) be a Borel pluripolar set.  Work
2224: on coordinate balls \(V\Subset V'\Subset U\), with \(V'\) strongly
2225: pseudoconvex.  Choose a smooth strictly psh function \(\rho\) on a
2226: neighbourhood of \(\overline{V'}\), and set \(\beta:=\ddc\rho\).  Recall
2227: that the Bedford--Taylor capacity and its outer capacity are
2228: \[
2229:  \Capa_{\mathrm{BT}}(E,V')
2230:  :=\sup_{\substack{q\in\PSH(V')\\0<q<1}}
2231:        \int_E(\ddc q)^n,
2232:  \qquad
2233:  \Capa_{\mathrm{BT}}^*(E,V')
2234:  :=\inf_{\substack{G\supset E\\G\ \mathrm{open}}}
2235:        \Capa_{\mathrm{BT}}(G,V').
2236: \]
2237: For fixed \(k\), every
2238: \(w_{j,k}:=\max\{u_j,-k\}\) is locally bounded and psh.  The mixed
2239: Bedford--Taylor measure
2240: \[
2241:  \nu_k:=\one_{O_k}\bigwedge_{j=1}^p\ddc w_{j,k}
2242:                    \wedge\beta^{n-p}
2243: \]
2244: vanishes on \(A\cap V\).  Indeed, each \(w_{j,k}\) is bounded on \(V'\)
2245: because \(\overline{V'}\Subset U\), and \(\rho\) is bounded there because
2246: it is smooth on a neighbourhood of \(\overline{V'}\).  After adding
2247: constants and multiplying by positive scalars, normalize the \(p\) functions
2248: \(w_{j,k}\) and the \(n-p\) copies of \(\rho\) to functions with values in
2249: \((0,1)\) on \(V'\).  Denote the normalized functions by
2250: \(f_i=a_i h_i+b_i\), where
2251: \((h_1,\ldots,h_n)=(w_{1,k},\ldots,w_{p,k},\rho,\ldots,\rho)\) and
2252: \(a_i>0\), and put \(W=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i\).  Positivity and
2253: multilinearity give
2254: \[
2255:  (\ddc W)^n\geq\frac{n!}{n^n}\bigwedge_{i=1}^n\ddc f_i
2256:  =\frac{n!}{n^n}\left(\prod_{i=1}^na_i\right)
2257:    \bigwedge_{j=1}^p\ddc w_{j,k}\wedge\beta^{n-p}.
2258: \]
2259: Consequently, for Borel \(E\subset V\),
2260: \[
2261:  \nu_k(E)\leq C_k\int_E(\ddc W)^n
2262:              \leq C_k\Capa_{\mathrm{BT}}^*(E,V').
2263: \]
2264: Here the first inequality also uses the fact that restriction by
2265: \(\one_{O_k}\) can only decrease a positive measure.  A pluripolar set has
2266: zero Bedford--Taylor outer capacity
2267: \cite[Theorem~6.9]{BT82}.  Finally, the currents in
2268: \eqref{eq:complex-npp-truncation} increase to the nonpluripolar product, so
2269: their trace measures \(\nu_k\) increase to its trace measure on \(V\).
2270: Continuity from below therefore gives
2271: \[
2272:  \left(\left\langle\bigwedge_{j=1}^p\ddc u_j\right\rangle
2273:        \wedge\beta^{n-p}\right)(A\cap V)
2274:  =\lim_k\nu_k(A\cap V)=0.
2275: \]
2276: Since \(V\) is arbitrary, the product charges no pluripolar set.
2277: 
2278: \emph{Monotonicity of total masses.}  If
2279: \(\varphi_j\preceq\psi_j\) for every \(j\), with \(\psi_j\) in the same
2280: class, then
2281: \[
2282:  \int_X\langle\theta_{\varphi_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge\theta_{\varphi_p}
2283:  \wedge\omega^{n-p}\rangle
2284:  \leq
2285:  \int_X\langle\theta_{\psi_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge\theta_{\psi_p}
2286:  \wedge\omega^{n-p}\rangle .
2287: \]
2288: This is \emph{not} a pointwise inequality between the two currents, and it
2289: is not proved by integration by parts on the truncations, because the
2290: error terms supported on the truncation boundaries do not obviously
2291: vanish.  The unrestricted statement is
2292: \cite[Theorem~1.1]{DDNL18mono}; its predecessor, under the hypothesis that
2293: the potentials have small unbounded locus, is
2294: \cite[Theorem~1.16]{BEGZ10}.  We import the former.
2295: 
2296: \emph{Bimeromorphic invariance.}  Let \(\pi:Y\to X\) be a modification
2297: with exceptional locus \(F\) and indeterminacy locus of \(\pi^{-1}\)
2298: equal to \(Z=\pi(F)\).  Both \(F\) and \(Z\) are pluripolar --- they are
2299: proper analytic subsets --- so no mass sits on them.  On the complement,
2300: \(\pi\) is a biholomorphism and the change-of-variables formula applies
2301: term by term to the truncations.  Hence each mixed total mass is
2302: preserved.  This is the statement used in
2303: \Cref{thm:tna-bimeromorphic}.
2304: 
2305: \begin{warning}{Monotonicity is about masses, not measures}
2306: \label{warn:ch51-monotonicity}
2307: \Cref{thm:complex-npp-ledger} asserts that replacing a potential by a
2308: less singular one in the same class can only increase the \emph{total}
2309: mixed masses.  It does not assert any inequality between the two
2310: Monge--Amp\`ere measures.  On \(\mathbf P^1\), take \(\varphi=\max\{G_0,
2311: -1\}\) and \(\psi=0\): both have mass \(1\), yet
2312: \(\MA_\omega(\varphi)\) charges a circle and \(\MA_\omega(\psi)=\omega\)
2313: does not.  This is computed in \Cref{ex:ch51-p1-envelope}.
2314: \end{warning}
2315: "}

2246: it is smooth on a neighbourhood of \(\overline{V'}\).  After adding
2247: constants and multiplying by positive scalars, normalize the \(p\) functions
2248: \(w_{j,k}\) and the \(n-p\) copies of \(\rho\) to functions with values in

2250: \(f_i=a_i h_i+b_i\), where

2260: \[

2279: \(\varphi_j\preceq\psi_j\) for every \(j\), with \(\psi_j\) in the same
2280: class, then

2296: \emph{Bimeromorphic invariance.}  Let \(\pi:Y\to X\) be a modification
2297: with exceptional locus \(F\) and indeterminacy locus of \(\pi^{-1}\)
2298: equal to \(Z=\pi(F)\).  Both \(F\) and \(Z\) are pluripolar --- they are
2299: proper analytic subsets --- so no mass sits on them.  On the complement,
2300: \(\pi\) is a biholomorphism and the change-of-variables formula applies
2301: term by term to the truncations.  Hence each mixed total mass is
2302: preserved.  This is the statement used in
2303: \Cref{thm:tna-bimeromorphic}.

2305: \begin{warning}{Monotonicity is about masses, not measures}
2306: \label{warn:ch51-monotonicity}

2308: less singular one in the same class can only increase the \emph{total}

2312: \(\MA_\omega(\varphi)\) charges a circle and \(\MA_\omega(\psi)=\omega\)
2313: does not.  This is computed in \Cref{ex:ch51-p1-envelope}.
2314: \end{warning}

2659: \section{The \texorpdfstring{\(P\)}{P}-envelope}
2660: \label{sec:ch51-p-envelope}
2661: 
2662: An envelope replaces a potential by the largest potential of a prescribed
2663: kind lying below it.  Two such operators are needed in
2664: \cref{part:complex}, and they are genuinely different.  The

2667: keeps only the multiplier ideals and maximizes.  Since the second
2668: constraint is weaker, the second envelope is larger,
2669: \eqref{eq:complex-p-i-comparison}, and the two can differ.

3353: \begin{proof}[The steps in full]
3354: Write \(F:=\{\psi\in\PSH(X,\theta)\mid\psi\leq0,\
3355: \psi\sim_{\mathcal I}\varphi\}\) for the competitor family in
3356: \eqref{eq:complex-i-envelope}.
3357: 
3358: \emph{Step 1: \(F\) is nonempty and directed.}  It contains
3359: \(\varphi-\sup_X\varphi\).  If \(\psi_1,\psi_2\in F\), then
3360: \(\max\{\psi_1,\psi_2\}\in\PSH(X,\theta)\) by
3361: \Cref{prop:ch51-psh-operations}, item \cref{itm:ch51-op:max}, it is
3362: \(\leq0\), and by \Cref{prop:ch51-lelong-calculus}, item
3363: \cref{itm:ch51-lc:max}, applied at a generic point of each prime divisor
3364: \(E\) over \(X\),
3365: \[
3366:  \nu(\max\{\psi_1,\psi_2\},E)
3367:  =\min\{\nu(\psi_1,E),\nu(\psi_2,E)\}
3368:  =\nu(\varphi,E).
3369: \]
3370: Hence \(\max\{\psi_1,\psi_2\}\in F\), and \(F\) is directed.
3371: 
3372: \emph{Step 2: the envelope lies in \(F\), which gives
3373: \eqref{eq:complex-i-projection}.}  By Step 1 and
3374: \Cref{lem:ch51-lelong-increasing},
3375: \[
3376:  \nu\bigl(P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I},E\bigr)
3377:  =\inf_{\psi\in F}\nu(\psi,E)
3378:  =\nu(\varphi,E)
3379: \]
3380: for every prime divisor \(E\) over \(X\).  Since
3381: \(P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}\leq0\), this says
3382: \(P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}\in F\); it is therefore the largest
3383: element of \(F\), and in particular
3384: \(\varphi\sim_{\mathcal I}P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}\).  As \(F\)
3385: depends only on the \(\mathcal I\)-class of \(\varphi\), the family
3386: attached to \(P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}\) is the same \(F\), and
3387: idempotence follows.
3388: 
3389: \emph{Step 3: \(\varphi\sim_{\mathcal I}P_\theta[\varphi]\).}  By Step 1
3390: of the proof of \Cref{thm:complex-p-projection}, the rooftops
3391: \(u_C=(\varphi+C)\wedge_\theta V_\theta\) satisfy \(u_C\sim\varphi\) for
3392: \(C\) large, hence \(\nu(u_C,E)=\nu(\varphi,E)\) for every \(E\) by
3393: \Cref{prop:ch51-lelong-calculus}, item \cref{itm:ch51-lc:bounded}.  The
3394: family \((u_C)\) is increasing, and
3395: \(P_\theta[\varphi]=\uscsup_Cu_C\); so
3396: \Cref{lem:ch51-lelong-increasing} gives
3397: \(\nu(P_\theta[\varphi],E)=\nu(\varphi,E)\), which is the second half of
3398: \eqref{eq:complex-p-i-comparison}.  This step uses no positivity of
3399: mass.
3400: 
3401: \emph{Step 4: \(P_\theta[\varphi]\leq P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}\).}
3402: By Step 3 and \(P_\theta[\varphi]\leq V_\theta\leq0\), the potential
3403: \(P_\theta[\varphi]\) belongs to \(F\); by Step 2 it is therefore at most
3404: the largest element of \(F\).
3405: 
3406: \emph{Step 5: analytic singularities.}  Assume \(\varphi\) has analytic
3407: singularities, and let \(\rho:Z\to X\) be a log resolution with
3408: \[
3409:  \rho^*\varphi=c\log|s_D|_h^2+O(1),
3410: \]
3411: \(D\) an effective divisor with simple normal crossing support, \(h\) a
3412: smooth metric on \(\cO_Z(D)\), and \(c>0\).  Put
3413: \(\Psi:=P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}\), which by Step 2 satisfies
3414: \(\Psi\sim_{\mathcal I}\varphi\).  By
3415: \Cref{prop:ch51-divisorial-calculus}, items
3416: \cref{itm:ch51-dc:pullback} and \cref{itm:ch51-dc:analytic}, for every
3417: prime divisor \(E\subset Z\),
3418: \[
3419:  \nu(\rho^*\Psi,E)=\nu(\Psi,E)=\nu(\varphi,E)=c\,\ord_E(D).
3420: \]
3421: The Siu decomposition of \Cref{sec:ch51-divisorial}, applied to the
3422: closed positive current \(\rho^*\theta+\ddc\rho^*\Psi\), therefore gives
3423: \[
3424:  \rho^*\theta+\ddc\rho^*\Psi\ \geq\ c\,[D].
3425: \]
3426: Writing \(\Theta_D=c_1(\cO_Z(D),h)\) and using Poincar\'e--Lelong
3427: \eqref{eq:appJ-complex-section-pl} in the form
3428: \(\ddc\log|s_D|_h^2=[D]-\Theta_D\), we obtain
3429: \[
3430:  \bigl(\rho^*\theta-c\,\Theta_D\bigr)

3435: \(\rho^*\Psi\leq c\log|s_D|_h^2+C=\rho^*\varphi+C'\), and since \(\rho\)

3498: \begin{corollary}\label{cor:complex-comparison-hierarchy}

3502:  \Longrightarrow

3512: \begin{proof}
3513: If \(\varphi\preceq\psi\), then every normalized competitor defining
3514: \(P_\theta[\varphi]\) is also a competitor for \(P_\theta[\psi]\), which
3515: gives the first implication.  The second follows from
3516: \eqref{eq:complex-p-i-comparison}: applying the \(\mathcal I\)-envelope
3517: to the ordered \(P\)-envelopes gives the corresponding
3518: \(\mathcal I\)-order.  Applying both implications in both directions

3300: \subsection{The envelope}
3301: \label{sec:ch51-i-envelope-def}
3302: 
3303: \begin{definition}[\(\mathcal I\)-envelope]
3304: \label{def:complex-i-envelope}
3305: For \(\varphi\in\PSH(X,\theta)\), set
3306: \[
3307:  P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}
3308:  :=\uscsup\{\psi\in\PSH(X,\theta)\mid
3309:           \psi\leq0,\ \psi\sim_{\mathcal I}\varphi\}.
3310: \tag{51.27}\label{eq:complex-i-envelope}
3311: \]
3312: It is \(\mathcal I\)-model if it is fixed by this operator.
3313: \end{definition}
3314: 
3315: \begin{theorem}\label{thm:complex-i-projection}
3316: For every \(\varphi\in\PSH(X,\theta)\),
3317: \[
3318:  \varphi\sim_{\mathcal I}P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I},
3319: \qquad
3320:  P_\theta[P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}]_{\mathcal I}
3321:       =P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}.
3322: \tag{51.28}\label{eq:complex-i-projection}
3323: \]
3324: Furthermore,
3325: \[
3326:  P_\theta[\varphi]\leq P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I},
3327: \qquad
3328:  \varphi\sim_{\mathcal I}P_\theta[\varphi].
3329: \tag{51.29}\label{eq:complex-p-i-comparison}
3330: \]
3331: If \(\varphi\) has analytic singularities, then
3332: \[
3333:  \varphi\sim P_\theta[\varphi]
3334:         \sim P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}.
3335: \tag{51.30}\label{eq:complex-analytic-envelope-agreement}
3336: \]
3337: \end{theorem}
3338: 
3339: \begin{proof}
3340: Choquet reduction replaces the family in
3341: \eqref{eq:complex-i-envelope} by an increasing sequence.  Finite maxima
3342: preserve divisorial Lelong numbers, and strong openness shows that its
3343: usc supremum has the same multiplier ideals as \(\varphi\).  This proves
3344: \eqref{eq:complex-i-projection}.  Formula
3345: \eqref{eq:complex-p-envelope-rooftop}, again with strong openness, gives
3346: \(\varphi\sim_{\mathcal I}P_\theta[\varphi]\), hence
3347: \eqref{eq:complex-p-i-comparison}.  For analytic singularities, pass to
3348: a log resolution.  Divisorial orders then control the whole singularity
3349: up to \(O(1)\), so the two envelopes cannot be strictly less singular
3350: than \(\varphi\).
3351: \end{proof}
3352: 
3353: \begin{proof}[The steps in full]
3354: Write \(F:=\{\psi\in\PSH(X,\theta)\mid\psi\leq0,\
3355: \psi\sim_{\mathcal I}\varphi\}\) for the competitor family in
3356: \eqref{eq:complex-i-envelope}.
3357: 
3358: \emph{Step 1: \(F\) is nonempty and directed.}  It contains
3359: \(\varphi-\sup_X\varphi\).  If \(\psi_1,\psi_2\in F\), then
3360: \(\max\{\psi_1,\psi_2\}\in\PSH(X,\theta)\) by
3361: \Cref{prop:ch51-psh-operations}, item \cref{itm:ch51-op:max}, it is
3362: \(\leq0\), and by \Cref{prop:ch51-lelong-calculus}, item
3363: \cref{itm:ch51-lc:max}, applied at a generic point of each prime divisor
3364: \(E\) over \(X\),
3365: \[
3366:  \nu(\max\{\psi_1,\psi_2\},E)
3367:  =\min\{\nu(\psi_1,E),\nu(\psi_2,E)\}
3368:  =\nu(\varphi,E).
3369: \]
3370: Hence \(\max\{\psi_1,\psi_2\}\in F\), and \(F\) is directed.
3371: 
3372: \emph{Step 2: the envelope lies in \(F\), which gives
3373: \eqref{eq:complex-i-projection}.}  By Step 1 and
3374: \Cref{lem:ch51-lelong-increasing},
3375: \[
3376:  \nu\bigl(P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I},E\bigr)
3377:  =\inf_{\psi\in F}\nu(\psi,E)
3378:  =\nu(\varphi,E)
3379: \]
3380: for every prime divisor \(E\) over \(X\).  Since
3381: \(P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}\leq0\), this says
3382: \(P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}\in F\); it is therefore the largest
3383: element of \(F\), and in particular
3384: \(\varphi\sim_{\mathcal I}P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}\).  As \(F\)
3385: depends only on the \(\mathcal I\)-class of \(\varphi\), the family
3386: attached to \(P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}\) is the same \(F\), and
3387: idempotence follows.
3388: 
3389: \emph{Step 3: \(\varphi\sim_{\mathcal I}P_\theta[\varphi]\).}  By Step 1
3390: of the proof of \Cref{thm:complex-p-projection}, the rooftops
3391: \(u_C=(\varphi+C)\wedge_\theta V_\theta\) satisfy \(u_C\sim\varphi\) for
3392: \(C\) large, hence \(\nu(u_C,E)=\nu(\varphi,E)\) for every \(E\) by
3393: \Cref{prop:ch51-lelong-calculus}, item \cref{itm:ch51-lc:bounded}.  The
3394: family \((u_C)\) is increasing, and
3395: \(P_\theta[\varphi]=\uscsup_Cu_C\); so
3396: \Cref{lem:ch51-lelong-increasing} gives
3397: \(\nu(P_\theta[\varphi],E)=\nu(\varphi,E)\), which is the second half of
3398: \eqref{eq:complex-p-i-comparison}.  This step uses no positivity of
3399: mass.
3400: 
3401: \emph{Step 4: \(P_\theta[\varphi]\leq P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}\).}
3402: By Step 3 and \(P_\theta[\varphi]\leq V_\theta\leq0\), the potential
3403: \(P_\theta[\varphi]\) belongs to \(F\); by Step 2 it is therefore at most
3404: the largest element of \(F\).
3405: 
3406: \emph{Step 5: analytic singularities.}  Assume \(\varphi\) has analytic
3407: singularities, and let \(\rho:Z\to X\) be a log resolution with
3408: \[
3409:  \rho^*\varphi=c\log|s_D|_h^2+O(1),
3410: \]
3411: \(D\) an effective divisor with simple normal crossing support, \(h\) a
3412: smooth metric on \(\cO_Z(D)\), and \(c>0\).  Put
3413: \(\Psi:=P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}\), which by Step 2 satisfies
3414: \(\Psi\sim_{\mathcal I}\varphi\).  By
3415: \Cref{prop:ch51-divisorial-calculus}, items
3416: \cref{itm:ch51-dc:pullback} and \cref{itm:ch51-dc:analytic}, for every
3417: prime divisor \(E\subset Z\),
3418: \[
3419:  \nu(\rho^*\Psi,E)=\nu(\Psi,E)=\nu(\varphi,E)=c\,\ord_E(D).
3420: \]
3421: The Siu decomposition of \Cref{sec:ch51-divisorial}, applied to the
3422: closed positive current \(\rho^*\theta+\ddc\rho^*\Psi\), therefore gives
3423: \[
3424:  \rho^*\theta+\ddc\rho^*\Psi\ \geq\ c\,[D].
3425: \]
3426: Writing \(\Theta_D=c_1(\cO_Z(D),h)\) and using Poincar\'e--Lelong
3427: \eqref{eq:appJ-complex-section-pl} in the form
3428: \(\ddc\log|s_D|_h^2=[D]-\Theta_D\), we obtain
3429: \[
3430:  \bigl(\rho^*\theta-c\,\Theta_D\bigr)
3431:  +\ddc\bigl(\rho^*\Psi-c\log|s_D|_h^2\bigr)\ \geq\ 0 ,
3432: \]
3433: so \(\rho^*\Psi-c\log|s_D|_h^2\) is quasi-psh on the compact manifold
3434: \(Z\), hence bounded above.  Thus
3435: \(\rho^*\Psi\leq c\log|s_D|_h^2+C=\rho^*\varphi+C'\), and since \(\rho\)
3436: is an isomorphism over a dense open subset of \(X\) and both sides are
3437: upper semicontinuous, \(\Psi\preceq\varphi\).  Combining with
3438: \(\varphi\preceq P_\theta[\varphi]\leq\Psi\) from
3439: \Cref{prop:ch51-p-elementary}, item \cref{itm:ch51-pe:above}, and Step 4,
3440: \[
3441:  \varphi\ \sim\ P_\theta[\varphi]\ \sim\ P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I},
3442: \]
3443: which is \eqref{eq:complex-analytic-envelope-agreement}.
3444: \end{proof}
3445: 
3446: \begin{corollary}[Canonical reconstruction from realizable
3447: \texorpdfstring{\(\mathcal I\)}{I}-data]
3448: \label{cor:ch51-i-canonical-reconstruction}
3449: For a realizable \(\mathcal I\)-class
3450: \(d=[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}\) in \(\PSH(X,\theta)\), the formula
3451: \[
3452:  \mathcal R_\theta(d):=P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}
3453: \]
3454: is well defined.  It is the unique \(\mathcal I\)-model potential in the
3455: class \(d\) with \(\sup_X\mathcal R_\theta(d)=0\).  Thus realizable
3456: \(\mathcal I\)-data determines its canonical normalized
3457: \(\mathcal I\)-model representative, without a positive-mass hypothesis.
3458: \end{corollary}
3459: 
3460: \begin{proof}
3461: The competitor family in \eqref{eq:complex-i-envelope} depends only on
3462: \(d\).  The proof of \Cref{thm:complex-i-projection} shows that its
3463: envelope lies in that family and is its largest element; the formula is
3464: therefore well defined.  The second identity in that theorem says that the
3465: output is \(\mathcal I\)-model.  It is at most zero by
3466: \eqref{eq:complex-i-envelope}.  If its supremum were strictly negative,
3467: adding a sufficiently small positive constant would give another competitor
3468: in the same defining family, contradicting maximality.  Finally, a
3469: normalized \(\mathcal I\)-model potential in the class \(d\) is the fixed
3470: point of the envelope attached to that same competitor family, and hence is
3471: \(\mathcal R_\theta(d)\).
3472: \end{proof}
3473: 
3474: \begin{remark}[Where each hypothesis is used]
3475: \label{rem:ch51-i-projection-hypotheses}
3476: Steps 1--4 use no positivity of mass and no regularity of \(\varphi\);
3477: they are consequences of \Cref{lem:ch51-lelong-increasing} and the
3478: minimum rule for maxima.  Step 5 uses resolution of singularities and
3479: Siu's decomposition, and it is the only step that upgrades an
3480: \(\mathcal I\)-statement to an ordinary-type statement.  It is essential
3481: that the upgrade is applied to the \emph{envelope} \(\Psi\) and not to an
3482: arbitrary competitor: the argument produces a constant \(C'\) depending
3483: on \(\Psi\), and no uniform constant over the whole family \(F\) is
3484: claimed or needed.
3485: \end{remark}
3486: 
3487: \begin{warning}{Do not read Step 5 as a general rigidity statement}
3488: \label{warn:ch51-step5}
3489: Step 5 does \emph{not} say that two potentials with the same divisorial
3490: Lelong numbers have bounded difference.  It says that the
3491: \(\mathcal I\)-envelope of a potential with analytic singularities has
3492: bounded difference from it.  The general statement is false, by
3493: \Cref{ex:ch51-disk-three-types}; and the difference is not merely
3494: cosmetic, since \Cref{ex:ch51-cantor} produces an
3495: \(\mathcal I\)-equivalent pair with different nonpluripolar masses.
3496: \end{warning}
3497: 
3498: \begin{corollary}\label{cor:complex-comparison-hierarchy}
3499: For quasi-psh functions,
3500: \[
3501:  \varphi\preceq\psi
3502:  \Longrightarrow
3503:  \varphi\preceq_P\psi
3504:  \Longrightarrow
3505:  \varphi\preceq_{\mathcal I}\psi.
3506: \tag{51.31}\label{eq:complex-comparison-hierarchy}
3507: \]
3508: Neither reverse implication is asserted.  In particular,
3509: \(\mathcal I\)-equivalence is coarser than \(P\)-equivalence.
3510: \end{corollary}
3511: 
3512: \begin{proof}
3513: If \(\varphi\preceq\psi\), then every normalized competitor defining
3514: \(P_\theta[\varphi]\) is also a competitor for \(P_\theta[\psi]\), which
3515: gives the first implication.  The second follows from
3516: \eqref{eq:complex-p-i-comparison}: applying the \(\mathcal I\)-envelope
3517: to the ordered \(P\)-envelopes gives the corresponding
3518: \(\mathcal I\)-order.  Applying both implications in both directions
3519: gives the assertion about equivalence relations.
3520: \end{proof}
3521: 
3522: \begin{proof}[The second implication, in detail]
3523: Assume \(\varphi\preceq_P\psi\), that is
3524: \(P_\theta[\varphi]\leq P_\theta[\psi]\) for a common background in which
3525: both have positive mass.  Monotonicity of Lelong numbers under the
3526: pointwise order, which is \eqref{eq:complex-lelong-number}, gives
3527: \[
3528:  \nu\bigl(P_\theta[\varphi],E\bigr)
3529:  \ \geq\
3530:  \nu\bigl(P_\theta[\psi],E\bigr)
3531: \]
3532: for every prime divisor \(E\) over \(X\), the inequality reversing
3533: because a smaller potential is more singular.  By Step 3 of the proof of
3534: \Cref{thm:complex-i-projection}, the two sides equal
3535: \(\nu(\varphi,E)\) and \(\nu(\psi,E)\) respectively.  Hence
3536: \[
3537:  \nu(\varphi,E)\ \geq\ \nu(\psi,E)
3538:  \qquad\text{for every prime divisor }E\text{ over }X,
3539: \]
3540: which by \Cref{thm:complex-strong-openness}, item
3541: \cref{itm:ch51-so:equivalence}, and
3542: \Cref{def:complex-i-preorder} is exactly
3543: \(\varphi\preceq_{\mathcal I}\psi\).  Note that the conclusion does not
3544: mention \(\theta\), consistently with
3545: \Cref{prop:ch51-i-calculus}, item \cref{itm:ch51-ic:preorder}.
3546: \end{proof}
3547: 
3548: \begin{corollary}\label{cor:ch51-quotient-maps}
3549: There are canonical surjections of preordered sets
3550: \[
3551:  \QPSH(X)/{\sim}
3552:  \ \longrightarrow\
3553:  \QPSH(X)/{\sim_P}
3554:  \ \longrightarrow\
3555:  \QPSH(X)/{\sim_{\mathcal I}} ,
3556: \]
3557: where the middle quotient is taken on the locus of potentials of
3558: positive mass in a fixed sufficiently positive background.  Both maps are
3559: strictly non-injective:
3560: \Cref{ex:appH-loglog} separates the first two, and
3561: \Cref{ex:ch51-cantor} separates the last two.
3562: \end{corollary}
3563: 
3564: \begin{proof}
3565: The maps exist and are order preserving by
3566: \Cref{cor:complex-comparison-hierarchy}, and they are surjective because
3567: each is induced by the identity on representatives.  The separations are
3568: the cited examples.
3569: \end{proof}
3570: 
3571: The chain of \Cref{cor:ch51-quotient-maps} is the source of the
3572: factorization \eqref{eq:verified-trace-factorization}: the trace of
3573: \Cref{chap:operations-trace} depends only on the input
3574: \(\mathcal I\)-class but lands in a well-defined output \(P\)-class.
3575: Hence the map obtained by starting with input \(P\)-classes factors through
3576: the second surjection above.  \Cref{thm:verified-trace-factorization}
3577: records this asymmetric, source-backed factorization.

{"source_id":"p148_ch51_dependency_v4","source_sha256":"7f2b4890d6332d042113d89bfa921f0f58bbfcbd63c5a18a9eff21469a0fc40b","start_line":3793,"end_line":3933,"text":"3793: \subsection{A potential that is
3794: \texorpdfstring{\(\mathcal I\)}{I}-equivalent, but not
3795: \texorpdfstring{\(P\)}{P}-equivalent, to zero}
3796: \label{sec:ch51-cantor}
3797: 
3798: The construction uses one classical input: a compact set of vanishing
3799: logarithmic capacity carrying a probability measure without atoms.  We
3800: recall it explicitly so that the numbers below can be checked.
3801: 
3802: \begin{lemma}\label{lem:ch51-polar-cantor}
3803: Let \((\ell_m)_{m\geq0}\) be lengths with \(\ell_0=1\) and
3804: \(\ell_{m+1}\leq\ell_m/2\), and let
3805: \(F=\bigcap_mF_m\subset[0,1]\subset\mathbf C\) be the generalized Cantor
3806: set in which \(F_m\) is a disjoint union of \(2^m\) closed intervals of
3807: length \(\ell_m\), each containing two intervals of the next stage.  Let
3808: \(\mu\) be the measure giving each of the \(2^m\) intervals of \(F_m\)
3809: mass \(2^{-m}\).  Then \(\mu\) is a nonatomic Borel probability measure
3810: carried by \(F\), and if
3811: \[
3812:  \sum_{m\geq0}2^{-m}\log\frac{1}{\ell_m}=+\infty ,
3813: \]
3814: then \(F\) has vanishing logarithmic capacity, hence is polar.  The
3815: choice \(\ell_0=1\) and \(\ell_m=\rme^{-4^m}\) for \(m\geq1\)
3816: satisfies both hypotheses, since the summands for \(m\geq1\) equal \(2^m\).
3817: \end{lemma}
3818: 
3819: \begin{proof}[Classical, with the divergence check]
3820: The measure \(\mu\) is the weak limit of the normalized Lebesgue measures
3821: on \(F_m\); it is nonatomic because every point of \(F\) lies in nested
3822: intervals of \(\mu\)-mass \(2^{-m}\to0\).  The capacity criterion for
3823: generalized Cantor sets is \cite[p.~31]{Car83}: the set is polar exactly
3824: when the displayed series diverges.  With \(\ell_0=1\) and
3825: \(\ell_m=\rme^{-4^m}\) for \(m\geq1\), one has
3826: \(\ell_1/\ell_0=\rme^{-4}\leq1/2\); for \(m\geq1\),
3827: \(\ell_{m+1}/\ell_m=\rme^{-3\cdot4^m}\leq1/2\) and
3828: \(2^{-m}\log(1/\ell_m)=2^m\), so the series diverges.
3829: \end{proof}
3830: 
3831: \begin{example}[\(\mathcal I\)-equivalent, not \(P\)-equivalent]
3832: \label{ex:ch51-cantor}
3833: Let \(X=\mathbf P^1\) with \(\omega=\ddc\log(1+|z|^2)\), normalized by
3834: \(\int_X\omega=1\), and let \(G_p\) be the Green function of
3835: \Cref{sec:ch51-unit-tests}, so that
3836: \[
3837:  G_p(z)=\log\frac{|z-p|^2}{(1+|z|^2)(1+|p|^2)}\leq0,
3838:  \qquad
3839:  \omega+\ddc G_p=\delta_p .
3840: \]
3841: Let \(F\) and \(\mu\) be as in \Cref{lem:ch51-polar-cantor}, and set
3842: \[
3843:  G_\mu(z):=\int_XG_p(z)\,\rd\mu(p).
3844: \]
3845: 
3846: For \(0\leq s\leq1\), put \(\varphi_s:=sG_\mu\).
3847: 
3848: \emph{The \(\varphi_s\) are genuine potentials.}  Each \(G_p\leq0\), so
3849: \(G_\mu\leq0\).  For \(z\) at chordal distance at least \(\delta\) from
3850: \(F\) one has \(G_p(z)\geq2\log\delta\) for every \(p\in F\), so
3851: \(G_\mu(z)\geq2\log\delta>-\infty\); in particular
3852: \(G_\mu\not\equiv-\infty\).  Fubini gives
3853: \[
3854:  \omega+\ddc G_\mu=\mu ,
3855:  \qquad
3856:  \omega+\ddc\varphi_s=(1-s)\omega+s\mu\ \geq0,
3857: \]
3858: so \(\varphi_s\in\PSH(X,\omega)\) with \(\varphi_s\leq0\).
3859: 
3860: \emph{All Lelong numbers vanish.}  On a Riemann surface every
3861: modification is an isomorphism, so the prime divisors over \(X\) are the
3862: points of \(X\), and
3863: \Cref{prop:ch51-lelong-three}, item \cref{itm:ch51-lelong:mass}, gives
3864: \[
3865:  \nu(\varphi_s,x)=(\omega+\ddc\varphi_s)(\{x\})
3866:  =(1-s)\omega(\{x\})+s\mu(\{x\})=0
3867: \]
3868: for every \(x\), because \(\omega\) is smooth and \(\mu\) is nonatomic.
3869: By \Cref{thm:complex-strong-openness}, item
3870: \cref{itm:ch51-so:equivalence}, or directly by Skoda's bound
3871: \Cref{prop:ch51-lelong-calculus}, item \cref{itm:ch51-lc:smooth}, applied
3872: to \(m\varphi_s\) for every \(m\),
3873: \[
3874:  \mathcal I(m\varphi_s)=\cO_X\quad(m\geq1),
3875:  \qquad\text{hence}\qquad
3876:  \varphi_s\sim_{\mathcal I}0 .
3877: \]
3878: 
3879: \emph{The nonpluripolar mass is \(1-s\).}  The set \(F\) is polar,
3880: hence pluripolar, and \(\mu(F)=1\).  Also \(\omega(F)=0\), since \(F\)
3881: has vanishing Lebesgue measure.  By
3882: \Cref{lem:ch51-npp-bidegree-one} and
3883: \Cref{thm:complex-npp-ledger}, the nonpluripolar product charges no
3884: pluripolar set, so
3885: \[
3886:  \MA_\omega(\varphi_s)
3887:  =\one_{X\setminus F}\bigl((1-s)\omega+s\mu\bigr)
3888:  =(1-s)\omega,
3889:  \qquad
3890:  M_\omega(\varphi_s)=1-s .
3891: \]
3892: The envelope of \(0\) is \(0\), since \(0\) is a competitor and every
3893: competitor is at most zero.  Thus one \(\mathcal I\)-class carries every
3894: mass in \([0,1]\), while
3895: \Cref{cor:ch51-i-canonical-reconstruction} identifies its canonical
3896: normalized \(\mathcal I\)-model representative with \(0\), of mass one.
3897: 
3898: \emph{Conclusion: \(\varphi_{1/2}\not\sim_P0\).}  Both
3899: \(\varphi_{1/2}\) and \(0\)
3900: have positive mass in the K\"ahler class \(\{\omega\}\), so
3901: \Cref{thm:complex-p-projection} applies to both and
3902: \Cref{thm:ch51-hierarchy-strict}, item \cref{itm:ch51-hs:mass}, gives:
3903: if \(\varphi_{1/2}\sim_P0\), then
3904: \(M_\omega(\varphi_{1/2})=M_\omega(0)\), that is \(\tfrac12=1\).  Hence
3905: \[
3906:  \varphi_{1/2}\sim_{\mathcal I}0,
3907:  \qquad
3908:  \varphi_{1/2}\not\sim_P0,
3909:  \qquad
3910:  \varphi_{1/2}\not\sim0 .
3911: \]

3913: \(M_\omega(P_\omega[\varphi_{1/2}])=\tfrac12\) and
3914: \(P_\omega[0]=V_\omega=0\) with mass \(1\), so the two envelopes differ.
3915: Since \(\omega+\ddc P_\omega[\varphi_{1/2}]\) has total mass \(1\) and
3916: nonpluripolar mass \(\tfrac12\), it carries mass \(\tfrac12\) on a polar
3917: set; in particular \(P_\omega[\varphi_{1/2}]\) is unbounded, although all its
3918: Lelong numbers vanish.
3919: 
3920: At the endpoint, \(\varphi_1\) has raw nonpluripolar mass zero but the
3921: same canonical normalized \(\mathcal I\)-model representative \(0\) has
3922: mass one.  Thus neither a raw zero-mass representative nor its raw mass can
3923: be reconstructed from its \(\mathcal I\)-class.
3924: 
3925: \emph{Direction of the failure.}  One implication does survive:
3926: \(\varphi_{1/2}\leq0\) gives \(\varphi_{1/2}\preceq0\), hence
3927: \(\varphi_{1/2}\preceq_P0\).  What fails is the reverse comparison
3928: \(0\preceq_P\varphi_{1/2}\), even though
3929: \(0\preceq_{\mathcal I}\varphi_{1/2}\) holds.
3930: So the second arrow in \eqref{eq:complex-comparison-hierarchy} is not
3931: reversible, and it is not reversible even after restricting to potentials
3932: of positive mass in a K\"ahler class on a curve.
3933: \end{example}"}
