3793: \subsection{A potential that is
3794: \texorpdfstring{\(\mathcal I\)}{I}-equivalent, but not
3795: \texorpdfstring{\(P\)}{P}-equivalent, to zero}
3796: \label{sec:ch51-cantor}
3797: 
3798: The construction uses one classical input: a compact set of vanishing
3799: logarithmic capacity carrying a probability measure without atoms.  We
3800: recall it explicitly so that the numbers below can be checked.
3801: 
3802: \begin{lemma}\label{lem:ch51-polar-cantor}
3803: Let \((\ell_m)_{m\geq0}\) be lengths with \(\ell_0=1\) and
3804: \(\ell_{m+1}\leq\ell_m/2\), and let
3805: \(F=\bigcap_mF_m\subset[0,1]\subset\mathbf C\) be the generalized Cantor
3806: set in which \(F_m\) is a disjoint union of \(2^m\) closed intervals of
3807: length \(\ell_m\), each containing two intervals of the next stage.  Let
3808: \(\mu\) be the measure giving each of the \(2^m\) intervals of \(F_m\)
3809: mass \(2^{-m}\).  Then \(\mu\) is a nonatomic Borel probability measure
3810: carried by \(F\), and if
3811: \[
3812:  \sum_{m\geq0}2^{-m}\log\frac{1}{\ell_m}=+\infty ,
3813: \]
3814: then \(F\) has vanishing logarithmic capacity, hence is polar.  The
3815: choice \(\ell_0=1\) and \(\ell_m=\rme^{-4^m}\) for \(m\geq1\)
3816: satisfies both hypotheses, since the summands for \(m\geq1\) equal \(2^m\).
3817: \end{lemma}
3818: 
3819: \begin{proof}[Classical, with the divergence check]
3820: The measure \(\mu\) is the weak limit of the normalized Lebesgue measures
3821: on \(F_m\); it is nonatomic because every point of \(F\) lies in nested
3822: intervals of \(\mu\)-mass \(2^{-m}\to0\).  The capacity criterion for
3823: generalized Cantor sets is \cite[p.~31]{Car83}: the set is polar exactly
3824: when the displayed series diverges.  With \(\ell_0=1\) and
3825: \(\ell_m=\rme^{-4^m}\) for \(m\geq1\), one has
3826: \(\ell_1/\ell_0=\rme^{-4}\leq1/2\); for \(m\geq1\),
3827: \(\ell_{m+1}/\ell_m=\rme^{-3\cdot4^m}\leq1/2\) and
3828: \(2^{-m}\log(1/\ell_m)=2^m\), so the series diverges.
3829: \end{proof}
3830: 
3831: \begin{example}[\(\mathcal I\)-equivalent, not \(P\)-equivalent]
3832: \label{ex:ch51-cantor}
3833: Let \(X=\mathbf P^1\) with \(\omega=\ddc\log(1+|z|^2)\), normalized by
3834: \(\int_X\omega=1\), and let \(G_p\) be the Green function of
3835: \Cref{sec:ch51-unit-tests}, so that
3836: \[
3837:  G_p(z)=\log\frac{|z-p|^2}{(1+|z|^2)(1+|p|^2)}\leq0,
3838:  \qquad
3839:  \omega+\ddc G_p=\delta_p .
3840: \]
3841: Let \(F\) and \(\mu\) be as in \Cref{lem:ch51-polar-cantor}, and set
3842: \[
3843:  G_\mu(z):=\int_XG_p(z)\,\rd\mu(p).
3844: \]
3845: 
3846: For \(0\leq s\leq1\), put \(\varphi_s:=sG_\mu\).
3847: 
3848: \emph{The \(\varphi_s\) are genuine potentials.}  Each \(G_p\leq0\), so
3849: \(G_\mu\leq0\).  For \(z\) at chordal distance at least \(\delta\) from
3850: \(F\) one has \(G_p(z)\geq2\log\delta\) for every \(p\in F\), so
3851: \(G_\mu(z)\geq2\log\delta>-\infty\); in particular
3852: \(G_\mu\not\equiv-\infty\).  Fubini gives
3853: \[
3854:  \omega+\ddc G_\mu=\mu ,
3855:  \qquad
3856:  \omega+\ddc\varphi_s=(1-s)\omega+s\mu\ \geq0,
3857: \]
3858: so \(\varphi_s\in\PSH(X,\omega)\) with \(\varphi_s\leq0\).
3859: 
3860: \emph{All Lelong numbers vanish.}  On a Riemann surface every
3861: modification is an isomorphism, so the prime divisors over \(X\) are the
3862: points of \(X\), and
3863: \Cref{prop:ch51-lelong-three}, item \cref{itm:ch51-lelong:mass}, gives
3864: \[
3865:  \nu(\varphi_s,x)=(\omega+\ddc\varphi_s)(\{x\})
3866:  =(1-s)\omega(\{x\})+s\mu(\{x\})=0
3867: \]
3868: for every \(x\), because \(\omega\) is smooth and \(\mu\) is nonatomic.
3869: By \Cref{thm:complex-strong-openness}, item
3870: \cref{itm:ch51-so:equivalence}, or directly by Skoda's bound
3871: \Cref{prop:ch51-lelong-calculus}, item \cref{itm:ch51-lc:smooth}, applied
3872: to \(m\varphi_s\) for every \(m\),
3873: \[
3874:  \mathcal I(m\varphi_s)=\cO_X\quad(m\geq1),
3875:  \qquad\text{hence}\qquad
3876:  \varphi_s\sim_{\mathcal I}0 .
3877: \]
3878: 
3879: \emph{The nonpluripolar mass is \(1-s\).}  The set \(F\) is polar,
3880: hence pluripolar, and \(\mu(F)=1\).  Also \(\omega(F)=0\), since \(F\)
3881: has vanishing Lebesgue measure.  By
3882: \Cref{lem:ch51-npp-bidegree-one} and
3883: \Cref{thm:complex-npp-ledger}, the nonpluripolar product charges no
3884: pluripolar set, so
3885: \[
3886:  \MA_\omega(\varphi_s)
3887:  =\one_{X\setminus F}\bigl((1-s)\omega+s\mu\bigr)
3888:  =(1-s)\omega,
3889:  \qquad
3890:  M_\omega(\varphi_s)=1-s .
3891: \]
3892: The envelope of \(0\) is \(0\), since \(0\) is a competitor and every
3893: competitor is at most zero.  Thus one \(\mathcal I\)-class carries every
3894: mass in \([0,1]\), while
3895: \Cref{cor:ch51-i-canonical-reconstruction} identifies its canonical
3896: normalized \(\mathcal I\)-model representative with \(0\), of mass one.
3897: 
3898: \emph{Conclusion: \(\varphi_{1/2}\not\sim_P0\).}  Both
3899: \(\varphi_{1/2}\) and \(0\)
3900: have positive mass in the K\"ahler class \(\{\omega\}\), so
3901: \Cref{thm:complex-p-projection} applies to both and
3902: \Cref{thm:ch51-hierarchy-strict}, item \cref{itm:ch51-hs:mass}, gives:
3903: if \(\varphi_{1/2}\sim_P0\), then
3904: \(M_\omega(\varphi_{1/2})=M_\omega(0)\), that is \(\tfrac12=1\).  Hence
3905: \[
3906:  \varphi_{1/2}\sim_{\mathcal I}0,
3907:  \qquad
3908:  \varphi_{1/2}\not\sim_P0,
3909:  \qquad
3910:  \varphi_{1/2}\not\sim0 .
3911: \]
3912: Explicitly, \(P_\omega[\varphi_{1/2}]\) is a model potential with
3913: \(M_\omega(P_\omega[\varphi_{1/2}])=\tfrac12\) and
3914: \(P_\omega[0]=V_\omega=0\) with mass \(1\), so the two envelopes differ.
3915: Since \(\omega+\ddc P_\omega[\varphi_{1/2}]\) has total mass \(1\) and
3916: nonpluripolar mass \(\tfrac12\), it carries mass \(\tfrac12\) on a polar
3917: set; in particular \(P_\omega[\varphi_{1/2}]\) is unbounded, although all its
3918: Lelong numbers vanish.
3919: 
3920: At the endpoint, \(\varphi_1\) has raw nonpluripolar mass zero but the
3921: same canonical normalized \(\mathcal I\)-model representative \(0\) has
3922: mass one.  Thus neither a raw zero-mass representative nor its raw mass can
3923: be reconstructed from its \(\mathcal I\)-class.
3924: 
3925: \emph{Direction of the failure.}  One implication does survive:
3926: \(\varphi_{1/2}\leq0\) gives \(\varphi_{1/2}\preceq0\), hence
3927: \(\varphi_{1/2}\preceq_P0\).  What fails is the reverse comparison
3928: \(0\preceq_P\varphi_{1/2}\), even though
3929: \(0\preceq_{\mathcal I}\varphi_{1/2}\) holds.
3930: So the second arrow in \eqref{eq:complex-comparison-hierarchy} is not
3931: reversible, and it is not reversible even after restricting to potentials
3932: of positive mass in a K\"ahler class on a curve.
3933: \end{example}

record.search_query: For realizable multiplier-ideal singularity data of theta-plurisubharmonic potentials, the normalized I-envelope is well defined on I-equivalence classes, is the unique normalized I-model representative without a mass hypothesis, while raw nonpluripolar mass need not descend to the I-class.
search_evidence: The theorem search did not return this combined reconstruction-and-counterexample statement. The authenticated current Chapter 51 source, treated as an internal proof source rather than an external publication or prior acceptance, supplies and derives the exact interfaces used.

source_evidence.comparison: Lines 100--139 distinguish pointwise, ordinary, P-, and I-comparison; define I-comparison using every integral multiplier ideal; state that I-equivalence is strictly coarser and remembers divisorial data; and explicitly note the Cantor separation by different masses. Lines 141--169 fix connected compact Kähler, smooth theta, and distinguish positivity and zero-mass regimes.

Lines 1554--1695 give strong openness, reconstruction of each divisorial Lelong number from the ideal tower, equivalence of all integral ideals with all divisorial Lelong numbers, and the exact valuative criterion with one epsilon uniform over every divisor. Lines 1697--1707 warn that this package does not recover ordinary singularity type or mass.

Lines 2122--2155 prove in degree one that the nonpluripolar product is the ordinary positive current restricted to the finite locus. Lines 2175--2276 record plurifine locality and prove that the product charges no pluripolar set, exactly supporting the global mass computation.

Lines 3226--3238 define the I-preorder by all integral ideal inclusions and give the opposite-direction divisorial criterion. Lines 3253--3297 prove maximum closure, scaling, pullback, and increasing-envelope behavior via the minimum and increasing-limit Lelong formulas.

Lines 3303--3322 define the exact normalized competitor envelope and state projection/idempotence. Lines 3353--3387 give the full nonempty, maximum-directed, Choquet/Lelong preservation proof. Lines 3446--3471 establish well-definedness and uniqueness of the normalized I-model for realizable data without positive mass; lines 3474--3495 delimit the conclusion and reject general rigidity.

Lines 3802--3828 verify child fitting, the nonatomic probability, and divergent capacity series. Lines 3831--3896 construct the Green potentials, prove all Lelong numbers and all scaled multiplier ideals vanish, and compute mass 1-s. Lines 3920--3923 give the zero-mass endpoint with canonical model 0 of mass one.

record.contextual_definition_comparison: The Chapter 51 definitions exactly match the proof: PSH(X,theta) on a connected compact Kähler manifold, I-equivalence at all integral scales, normalized competitors <=0, usc supremum, and an I-model as a fixed point. Its nonpluripolar-product normalization and Fubini--Study normalization agree with the P^1 construction. The source repeatedly limits the reconstruction domain to realized classes.
record.applicability: Every object in the proof meets the Chapter 51 hypotheses. The envelope argument uses only steps explicitly stated to require neither positive mass nor regularity of the representative. The curve example lies in a Kähler class, uses a genuine probability-supported positive current, and falls under the degree-one product formula. The source does not extend the claim to formal data, all semivaluations, singular spaces, or transcendental all-mass order isomorphisms.

results.title: On Fabry's Gap Theorem
results.theorem:
Suppose that $f(z)=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}a_{k}z^{k}$ is a power series with radius of
convergence 1. Assume that there is a subsequence $k_{l}$ of indices, such that
$\limsup\sqrt[k_{l}]{a_{k_{l}}}=1$, and a constant $\theta>0$, such that the
following holds true: If $N_{l}$ denotes the number of indices $k$ within the
interval $[(1-\theta)k_{l},(1+\theta)k_{l}]$, such that $a_{k}\neq 0$, then
$N_{l}/k_{l}\rightarrow 0$. Then the circle $|z|=1$ is the natural boundary of $f$.

results.title: Null-controllability for weakly dissipative heat-like equations
results.theorem:
Let $(\tau_{n})_{n}\in(0,1)^{\mathbb{N}}$. Assume that $\sum_{n}\tau_{n}<+\infty$. Let $K$ be the associated Smith-Volterra-Cantor set and $\omega\coloneqq{\mathbb{R}}\setminus K$. There exist $c>0$, $C>0$ and $r_{0}>0$ such that for every $0<r<r_{0}$,



$\frac{1}{24}\ \sum_{\rule{0.0pt}{5.12358pt}\mathclap{k\geq\log_{2}(3\operatorname{Leb}(K)/r)}}\ \tau_{k}\leq\inf_{x\in{\mathbb{R}}}\dfrac{\operatorname{Leb}(\omega\cap B(x,r))}{\operatorname{Leb}(B(x,r))}\leq 6\ \sum_{\mathclap{\quad k\geq\log_{2}(\operatorname{Leb}(K)/4r)}}\ \tau_{k},$



where $\log_{2}$ is the base $2$ logarithm $\log_{2}(x)=\ln(x)/\ln(2)$.

results.title: The closed span of some Exponential system $E_{\Lambda}$ in the spaces $L^p(\gamma,\beta)$, properties of a Biorthogonal family to $E_{\Lambda}$ in $L^2(\gamma,\beta)$, Moment problems, and a differential equation of Carleson
results.theorem:
Consider a sequence $\Lambda=\{\lambda_{n}\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ of distinct non-zero complex numbers such that
$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}1/|\lambda_{n}|<\infty$ and $\sup_{n\in\mathbb{N}}|\arg\lambda_{n}|<\pi/2$.
Then its condensation index $c(\Lambda)$ is equal to zero if and only if $\Lambda$ is an interpolating variety for the space $A^{0}_{|z|}$.

results.title: Growth of Solutions of Second Order Linear Differential Equations
results.theorem:
Let $f(z)$ be an entire function satisfying $T(r,f)\sim\log M(r,f)$ in a set $E$ of positive upper logarithmic density. For given $0<c<\frac{1}{4}$ and $r\in E$, the set



$I_{r}=\{\theta\in[0,2\pi):\log|f(re^{\iota\theta})|\leq(1-c)\log M(r,f)\}$



has linear measure zero.

results.title: On Lagrange polynomials and the rate of approximation of planar sets by polynomial Julia sets
results.theorem:
If $E\subset\mathbb{C}$ is an infinite compact set and $(a_{n})$ is a pseudo Leja sequence in $E$ of Edrei growth $(C_{n})$, then
there exists a closed disk ${\mathbb{D}}$ of radius $\frac{1}{M_{n}}\log(2-\frac{1}{C_{n}})$ such that ${\mathbb{D}}\cap E\neq\emptyset$ and every point $z$ of ${\mathbb{D}}$ satisfies​ the inequality $C_{n}|w_{n}(z)|\geq\|w_{n}\|_{E}$.

results.title: Logarithm laws for equilibrium states in negative curvature
results.theorem:
Let $(Z,
u)$ be a measured space with finite nonzero measure. Let
$(A_{n})_{n\in{\mathbb{N}}}$ be a sequence of measurable subsets of $Z$ such that
there exists $c>0$ with $
u(A_{n}\cap A_{m})\leq c\;
u(A_{n})\,
u(A_{m})$
for all distinct $n,m$ in ${\mathbb{N}}$. Then $
u(\limsup_{n}A_{n})>0$
if and only if the series $\sum_{n\in{\mathbb{N}}}
u(A_{n})$ diverges.

record.location: Proof, generalized Cantor zero-capacity criterion: Kellay--Mashreghi formula (3.4)
record.search_query: A generalized Cantor subset of the unit circle obtained from 2^n arcs of length ell_n has logarithmic capacity zero if and only if the series sum over n of 2^{-n} log(1/ell_n) diverges.
search_evidence: The theorem search returned no exact capacity criterion. The pinned arXiv:1102.5596 source contains formula (3.4) with the same iff and the preceding construction constraints.

source_evidence.comparison: Lines 370--378 construct the two-child generalized Cantor set and require 2 ell_n+lambda_n=ell_{n-1}, so the proof's strict child-fitting inequalities give positive removed gaps. Lines 387--390 state that logarithmic capacity is zero iff sum 2^{-n}log(1/ell_n) diverges, exactly formula (3.4).

record.contextual_definition_comparison: The source takes the initial circle length ell_0=2pi. The proof makes a fixed linear rescaling to ell_0=1; logarithmic capacity is multiplied by the scale factor, so whether it is zero is unchanged, and the convergence/divergence test is unchanged up to a finite constant contribution.
record.applicability: For ell_m=exp(-4^m), the fitting inequalities hold and each series term for m>=1 is 2^{-m}4^m=2^m, so the required divergence follows. The source criterion therefore makes the limiting compact set capacity zero.
record.detail: The exact source formula and construction match the proof. The proof additionally supplies the necessary fitting calculation and independently proves the limiting measure is nonatomic.

results.title: Dynamics in several complex variables: endomorphisms of projective spaces and polynomial-like mapping
results.theorem:
Let $u_{1},\ldots,u_{p}$, $p\leq k$, be locally bounded p.s.h. functions on
$X$. Then, the current ${dd^{c}}u_{1}\wedge\ldots\wedge{dd^{c}}u_{p}$
has no mass on locally pluripolar sets, in particular on
proper analytic sets of $X$.

results.title: Dynamical properties of families of holomorphic mapping
results.theorem: Let $u_{1},\ldots,u_{p}$, $p\leq k$, be locally bounded p.s.h. functions on $X$. Then the current $dd^{c}u_{1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dd^{c}u_{q}$ has no mass on locally pluripolar sets, in particular, on proper analytic sets of $X$.

results.title: On a vanishing theorem due to Bogomolov
results.theorem:
For $j=1,\cdots,p$, let $T_{j}$ and $T^{\prime}_{j}$ be two closed positive $(1,1)$-currents with small unbounded locus (i.e. there exists a (locally) complete pluripolar closed subset $A$ of $X$ outside which the potential is locally bounded) in the same cohomology class, and assume also that $T_{j}$ is less singular than $T^{\prime}_{j}$. Then the cohomology classes of their non-pluripolar products satisfy
$\{\langle T_{1}\wedge\cdots\wedge T_{p}\rangle\}\geq\{\langle T^{\prime}_{1}\wedge\cdots\wedge T^{\prime}_{p}\rangle\}$
in $H^{p,p}(X,\mathbb{R})$, where $\geq$ means that the difference is pseudo-effective, i.e. representable by a closed positive $(p,p)$-current.

results.title: Density and intersection of (1,1)-currents
results.theorem:
Let $T_{1},\cdots,T_{m}$ be positive closed $(1,1)-$currents with analytic singularities on a complex manifold $X$ whose supports have compact intersection. Denote by $Z_{j}$ the singular locus of $T_{j}$ and let $Z=\bigcup_{j=1}^{m}Z_{j}$. Then the non-pluripolar product $\langle T_{1}\wedge\cdots\wedge T_{m}\rangle$ is well-defined $X$ and



$\pi^{*}\langle T_{1}\wedge\cdots\wedge T_{m}\rangle=\mathbf{1}_{\pi^{-1}(X\setminus Z)}S,$



for any density current $S$ associated with $(T_{1},\ldots,T_{m})$.

results.title: Chern forms of hermitian metrics with analytic singularities on vector bundles
results.theorem:
Let $u_{1},\ldots,u_{m}$ be psh functions on a complex manifold $X$ such that the
unbounded locus $L(u_{j})$ is contained in analytic set $Z_{j}\subset X$ for
each $j$. Moreover, let $T$ be a closed positive current of
bidegree $(p,p)$ with support contained in an analytic set $W\subset X$.
Assume that



${\rm codim\,}(Z_{i_{1}}\cap\cdots\cap Z_{i_{\ell}}\cap W)\geq\ell+p$



for all choices of $1\leq i_{1}<\cdots<i_{\ell}\leq m$.
Then
$u_{m}dd^{c}u_{m-1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dd^{c}u_{1}\wedge T$ and
$dd^{c}u_{m}\wedge\cdots\wedge dd^{c}u_{1}\wedge T$ are well-defined and
have locally finite mass. The latter is a closed positive current.

results.title: Integration by parts formula for non-pluripolar product
results.theorem:
Let $\varphi_{1},\ldots,\varphi_{p}\in\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta)$ ($p\leq n$) be potentials with small unbounded loci. Let $A\subseteq X$ be a closed pluripolar set, such that $\varphi_{j}\in L^{\infty}_{\operatorname{loc}}(X-A)$ for $j=1,\ldots,p$. Then



$\theta_{\varphi_{1}}\wedge\cdots\wedge\theta_{\varphi_{p}}=\mathds{1}_{X-A}\,\theta_{\varphi_{1}|_{X-A}}\wedge\cdots\wedge\theta_{\varphi_{p}|_{X-A}}.$



On RHS, the product is the usual Bedford–Taylor product ([BT82]) on $X-A$, $\mathds{1}_{X-A}$ formally denotes the zero-extension to $X$.

results.title: Géométrie d'Arakelov des variétés toriques et fibrés en droites intégrables
results.theorem:
Soient $u_{1},\dots,u_{q}$ plurisousharmoniques sur $U$ et telles que pour tout $1\leqslant i\leqslant q$, $L(u_{i})$ est contenu dans un ensemble analytique $A_{i}\subset U$. Si pour tout choix d’indices $j_{1}<\dots j_{m}$ dans $\{1,\dots,q\}$, on a :



$\operatorname{codim}A_{j_{1}}\cap\dots\cap A_{j_{m}}\geqslant m,$



alors les courants $u_{1}(dd^{c}u_{2})\wedge\dots\wedge(dd^{c}u_{q})$ et $(dd^{c}u_{1})\wedge\dots\wedge(dd^{c}u_{q})$ sont bien définis et vérifient les
propriétés d’approximation énoncées au théorème (4.2.9).

results.title: Approximation and equidistribution results for pseudo-effective line bundles
results.theorem:
Let $U$ be an open set in ${\mathbb{C}}^{n}$,
$\Sigma$ be a proper analytic subset of $U$, and $u_{1},\ldots,u_{m}$ be psh functions on $U$
which are continuous on $U\setminus\Sigma$. Assume that $\dim\Sigma\leq n-m$
and that $u_{k,p}\,$, where $1\leq k\leq m$ and $p\geq 1$,
are psh functions on $U$ so that $u_{k,p}\to u_{k}$ locally uniformly on $U\setminus\Sigma$. Then
the currents $dd^{c}u_{1,p}\wedge\ldots\wedge dd^{c}u_{m,p}$
are well defined on $U$ for $p$ sufficiently enough, and
$dd^{c}u_{1,p}\wedge\ldots\wedge dd^{c}u_{m,p}\to dd^{c}u_{1}\wedge\ldots\wedge dd^{c}u_{m}$ weakly as $p\to\infty$ in the sense of currents on $U$.

results.title: Monge-Ampère measures on contact sets
results.theorem:
Let $\theta^{1},\ldots,\theta^{n}$ be smooth closed real $(1,1)$-forms on $X$ such that the cohomology classes
$\{\theta^{1}\},\ldots,\{\theta^{n}\}$ are pseudoeffectives. For $1\leq i\leq n$, let $\varphi_{i}$ be a $\theta^{i}$-psh function and $f_{i}$ be a $C^{1,\bar{1}}$ function on $X$ such that $\varphi_{i}\leq f_{i}$. Then the non-pluripolar product
$\theta^{1}_{\varphi_{1}}\wedge\ldots\wedge\theta^{n}_{\varphi_{n}}$ satisfies the equality:





${\bf 1}_{\bigcap_{j}\{\varphi_{j}=f_{j}\}}\theta^{1}_{\varphi_{1}}\wedge\ldots\wedge\theta^{n}_{\varphi_{n}}={\bf 1}_{\bigcap_{j}\{\varphi_{j}=f_{j}\}}\theta^{1}_{f_{1}}\wedge\ldots\wedge\theta^{n}_{f_{n}}$

(7)

results.title: Dynamics in several complex variables: endomorphisms of projective spaces and polynomial-like mapping
results.theorem:
Let $S$ be a positive closed $(p,p)$-current on $X$ and $u$ a
p.s.h. function on $X$. Assume that $S$ is locally moderate
and $u$ is Hölder continuous. Then the current ${dd^{c}}u\wedge S$ is
locally moderate. In particular, wedge-products of positive closed
$(1,1)$-currents with Hölder continuous local potentials are locally
moderate.

results.title: Equidistribution for non-pluripolar currents on compact Kähler manifolds
results.theorem:
If $u_{1},\cdots,u_{s}$ are psh functions on the complex manifold $X$, we shall say that the non-pluripolar product $\langle\bigwedge_{j=1}^{s}dd^{c}u_{j}\rangle$ is well defined on $X$ if for each compact subset $K$ of $X$, we have



$\displaystyle\sup_{k}\int_{K\cap O_{k}}\omega^{n-s}\wedge\bigwedge_{j=1}^{s}dd^{c}\max\{u_{j},-k\}<\infty.$



Then, the non-pluripolar product $\langle\bigwedge_{j=1}^{s}dd^{c}u_{j}\rangle$ is defined to be a current satisfying the following:


1.

$\mathbf{1}_{O_{k}}\langle\bigwedge_{j=1}^{s}dd^{c}u_{j}\rangle=\mathbf{1}_{O_{k}}\bigwedge_{j=1}^{s}dd^{c}\max\{u_{j},-k\}$;



2.

the current $\langle\bigwedge_{j=1}^{s}dd^{c}u_{j}\rangle$ has no mass on the pluripolar set



$X\setminus\bigcup_{k=1}^{\infty}O_{k}=\{u=-\infty\}.$

results.title: Super-potentials, densities of currents and number of periodic points for holomorphic maps
results.theorem: Let $T$ be a positive closed $(p,p)$-current on $X$ with a bounded super-potential. Then $T$ has no mass on pluripolar sets of $X$. In particular, it has no mass on proper analytic subsets of $X$.

results.title: Degenerate complex Monge-Amp\` ere type equations on compact Hermitian manifolds and applications
results.theorem:
It is easy to see that $O_{k}:=\{\varphi>\rho-k\}$ is a plurifine open subset, and for any compact subset $K$ of $X$,



$\displaystyle\sup_{k}\int_{K\cap O_{k}}(\beta+dd^{c}\varphi^{(k)})^{n}$
$\displaystyle\leq\sup_{k}\int_{X}(\beta+dd^{c}\varphi^{(k)})^{n}$





$\displaystyle=\int_{X}\beta^{n}<+\infty.$



Thus the Definition 2.1 of non-pluripolar product is well defined due to [BEGZ10, Definition 1.1], has basic properties in [BEGZ10, Proposition 1.4].

results.title: Monge-Ampère equations in big cohomology classes
results.theorem: Let $T_{1},...,T_{p}$ be closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on a complex manifold $X$ whose non-pluripolar product is well-defined. Then the positive $(p,p)$-current $\langle T_{1}\wedge...\wedge T_{p}\rangle$ is closed.

results.title: On a vanishing theorem due to Bogomolov
results.theorem:
For $j=1,\cdots,p$, let $T_{j}$ and $T^{\prime}_{j}$ be two closed positive $(1,1)$-currents with small unbounded locus (i.e. there exists a (locally) complete pluripolar closed subset $A$ of $X$ outside which the potential is locally bounded) in the same cohomology class, and assume also that $T_{j}$ is less singular than $T^{\prime}_{j}$. Then the cohomology classes of their non-pluripolar products satisfy
$\{\langle T_{1}\wedge\cdots\wedge T_{p}\rangle\}\geq\{\langle T^{\prime}_{1}\wedge\cdots\wedge T^{\prime}_{p}\rangle\}$
in $H^{p,p}(X,\mathbb{R})$, where $\geq$ means that the difference is pseudo-effective, i.e. representable by a closed positive $(p,p)$-current.

results.title: Uniform bounds for the Iitaka fibration
results.theorem:
For any positive integers $n$ and $\nu$, there exists an integer $m_{n,\nu}$ such that for any smooth complex projective variety $X$ of dimension $n$ with pseudo-effective canonical divisor, and any big and nef $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor $M$ on $X$ such that $\nu M$ is a $\mathbb{Z}$-divisor, the pluriadjoint map



$\phi_{m(K_{X}+M)}:X\dashrightarrow\mathbb{P}H^{0}(X,\mathcal{O}_{X}(m(K_{X}+M)))$



is birational for all $m\geq m_{n,\nu}$ divisible by $\nu$.

results.title: Numerical characterization of the hard Lefschetz classes of dimension two
results.theorem:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety of dimension $n$, and let $\mathfrak{L}=(L_{1},...,L_{n-2})$ be a critical collection of nef classes on $X$. Then for any big movable class $B$ on $X$, there is a unique big and movable class $M$ such that



$B\cdot\mathfrak{L}=\langle M^{n-1}\rangle,$



where $\langle-\rangle$ is the positive product of pseudo-effective classes.

results.title: On the uniformity of the Iitaka fibration
results.theorem:
For any positive integers $n$ and ${\nu}$, there exists an integer $m_{n,{\nu}}$ such that for any smooth complex projective
variety $Y$ of dimension $n$ with pseudo-effective
canonical divisor, and any big and nef ${\bf Q}$-Cartier divisor $M$ on $Y$ such that
${\nu}M$ is integral, the pluriadjoint map



$\varphi_{m(K_{Y}+M)}:Y\dashrightarrow{\bf P}H^{0}(Y,{\mathscr{O}}_{Y}(m(K_{Y}+M)))^{*}$



is birational onto its image, for all $m\geq m_{n,{\nu}}$ divisible by ${\nu}$.

results.title: Abundance for varieties with many differential forms
results.theorem:
Let $X$ be a projective manifold with $K_{X}\sim_{\mathbb{Q}}0$ and let $\mathcal{L}$ be a nef line bundle on $X$ with $\nu(X,\mathcal{L})=1$. Let $\eta\colon\widetilde{X}\to X$ be a finite étale cover such that the Beauville-Bogomolov decomposition is of the form



$\widetilde{X}\simeq T\times\prod X_{j},$



where the $X_{j}$ are even-dimensional Calabi-Yau manifolds or hyperkähler manifolds, and $T$ is an abelian variety. Then
there exists a line bundle $\mathcal{L}^{\prime}$ numerically equivalent to $\mathcal{L}$ such that $\kappa(X,\mathcal{L}^{\prime})\geq 0$.

results.title: Rings of Siegel-Jacobi forms of bounded relative index are not finitely generated
results.theorem:
Let $(L,h)$ be a line bundle with a toroidal psh metric with
singularity divisor $D$, and
$s$ a non-zero rational section of $L$. If $\mathbb{D}(L,s,h)$ is nef and big and for every
irreducible component $D_{i}$ of $D$ the condition
$\operatorname{ord}_{D_{i}}(\mathbb{D}(L,s,h))>0$ holds, then



$\operatorname{b\text{-}div}(\mathcal{R}(L,s,h))=\mathbb{D}(L,s,h).$

results.title: Codimension one foliations with numerically trivial canonical class on singular spaces
results.theorem:
Let $X$ be a normal complex quasi-projective variety with klt singularities, let $1\leqslant p\leqslant\dim X$ be an integer,
and let $\mathscr{A}\subseteq\Omega_{X}^{[p]}$ be a saturated reflexive subsheaf of rank one.
Suppose that $\mathscr{A}^{[m]}$ is a line bundle for some positive integer $m$.
Let $\beta\colon Z\to X$ be a resolution of singularities with exceptional set $E$, and assume that $E$ is a divisor with simple normal crossings.
Let $\mathscr{B}\subseteq\Omega_{Z}^{p}$ denotes the saturation of $\beta^{[*]}\mathscr{A}\subseteq\Omega_{Z}^{p}$, and let $E_{1}$ denotes
the reduced divisor on $Z$ whose support is
the union of all irreducible components $E^{\prime}$ of $E$ such that $\mathscr{B}$ is not saturated in $\Omega_{Z}^{p}\big{(}\textup{log}\,E\big{)}$ at general points of $E^{\prime}$.
Then, there exist an effective $\beta$-exceptional divisor $E_{2}$ and a rational number
$0\leqslant\varepsilon<1$ such that $\beta^{*}c_{1}(\mathscr{A})+E_{2}\sim_{\mathbb{Q}}c_{1}(\mathscr{B})+\varepsilon E_{1}$.

results.title: On the uniformity of the Iitaka fibration
results.theorem:
Let $n$ and ${\nu}$ be positive integers. Suppose there exists a positive constant $v$ such that, for any smooth projective
variety $V$ of dimension $<n$ with pseudo-effective canonical divisor, and any big
and nef ${\bf Q}$-Cartier divisor $N$ on $V$
such that
${\nu}N$ is integral,
we have $\mathop{\rm vol}\nolimits(K_{V}+N)\geq v$. Then, there exists two positive constants $a:=a_{n,{\nu}}$ and
$b:=b_{n,{\nu}}$ such that,
for any smooth projective
variety $Y$ of dimension $n$ with pseudo-effective canonical divisor, and any big and
nef ${\bf Q}$-Cartier divisor $M$ on $Y$ such that
${\nu}M$ is integral, the rational pluriadjoint map



$\varphi_{m(K_{Y}+M)}:Y\dashrightarrow{\bf P}H^{0}(Y,{\mathscr{O}}_{Y}(m(K_{Y}+M)))^{*}$



is birational onto its image, for all



$m\geq a+{b\over\mathop{\rm vol}\nolimits(K_{Y}+M)^{1/n}}$



such that $mM$ is integral.

results.title: On effective non-vanishing and base-point-freeness
results.theorem:
Let $X$ and $S$ be smooth projective varieties,
let $f:X\to S$ be a surjective morphism,
and let $B$ be an effective $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor on $X$
whose support is a normal crossing divisor and whose coefficients are
strictly less than $1$.
Assume that there exists a normal crossing divisor $\Gamma$ on $S$
such that $f$ is smooth and $\mathrm{Supp}(B)$ is relative
normal crossing over $S_{0}=S\setminus\Gamma$.
Let $D$ be a Cartier divisor on $X$.
Assume that $D\sim_{\mathbb{Q}}K_{X/S}+B$.
Then the following hold:


(1) $\mathcal{F}=f_{*}\mathcal{O}_{X}(D)$ is a locally free sheaf.


(2) Let $\pi:P=\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{F})\to S$ be the associated
projective space bundle, and let $P_{0}=\pi^{-1}(S_{0})$.
Then the tautological invertible sheaf $\mathcal{O}_{P}(1)$ on
$P$ has a singular hermitian metric $h$ which is smooth over $P_{0}$
and such that the curvature current $\Theta$ is semipositive and that
the corresponding multiplier ideal sheaf coincides with
$\mathcal{O}_{P}$.


(3) There exists a finite surjective morphism $\sigma:S^{\prime}\to S$ from a
smooth projective variety $S^{\prime}$ such that $\Gamma^{\prime}=\sigma^{-1}(\Gamma)$ is a
normal crossing
divisor and satisfies the following conditions:
Let $X^{\prime}\to X\times_{S}S^{\prime}$ be a birational morphism from a smooth projective
variety which is isomorphic over $S_{0}$ and such that
the union of the pull-back of
the support of $B$, the pull-back of the support of $\Gamma$ and
the exceptional locus is a normal crossing divisor.
Let $f^{\prime}:X^{\prime}\to S^{\prime}$ and $\tau:X^{\prime}\to X$ be the induced morphisms.
An effective $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor $B^{\prime}$ on $X^{\prime}$
is defined such that its coefficients are strictly
less than $1$ and that $R=\tau^{*}(K_{X/S}+B)-(K_{X^{\prime}/S^{\prime}}+B^{\prime})$ is a
divisor.
Let $D^{\prime}=\tau^{*}D-R$.
Then $R$ is effective,
and the assumptions of the theorem are satisfied by $f^{\prime}:X^{\prime}\to S^{\prime}$, $B^{\prime}$
and $D^{\prime}$.
The locally free sheaf $\mathcal{F}^{\prime}=f^{\prime}_{*}\mathcal{O}_{X^{\prime}}(D^{\prime})$ on $S^{\prime}$
satisfies that $\sigma^{*}\mathcal{F}\supset\mathcal{F}^{\prime}$.
The singular hermitian metric $h$ induces a singular hermitian metric $h^{\prime}$
on the tautological invertible sheaf
$\mathcal{O}_{P^{\prime}}(1)$ on $P^{\prime}=\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{F}^{\prime})$,
and the Lelong number of the curvature current $\Theta^{\prime}$
vanishes at any point of $P^{\prime}$.
In particular, $\mathcal{F}^{\prime}$ is numerically semipositive.
If $\Theta^{\prime}$ is strictly positive at a point on $P^{\prime}_{0}$, then
$\mathcal{O}_{P^{\prime}}(1)$ is also big.

results.title: Wonderful resolutions and categorical crepant resolutions of singularities
results.theorem:
Let $X$ be an algebraic variety with Gorenstein rational singularities. Let $\pi:\tilde{X}\rightarrow X$ be a resolution of singularities such that the exceptional divisor $E$ of $\pi$ is irreducible, smooth and flat over $\pi(E)$. Then there exists a positive integer $m$ such that:





$K_{\tilde{X}}=K_{X}\otimes\mathscr{O}_{\tilde{X}}(mE),$



and we have a semi-orthogonal decomposition:



$\mathrm{D^{b}}(E)=\langle\mathscr{O}_{E}(mE)\otimes B_{m},\ldots,\mathscr{O}_{E}(E)\otimes B_{1},B_{0}\rangle,$



with $\mathrm{\textbf{L}}\pi^{*}\mathrm{D^{perf}}(\pi(E))\subset B_{m}\subset\cdots\subset B_{1}\subset B_{0}$.

results.title: Bijectiveness of the Nash Map for Quasi-Ordinary Hypersurface Singularities
results.theorem:
Let $(X,x)$ be a irreducible germ of quasi-ordinary hypersurface
singularity. Let $B$ a closed subscheme verifying Hypothesis 1.
Then the Nash map between the set of Nash components of
$\pi_{X}^{-1}(B)$ and the set of essential divisors of $X$ relative
to $B$ is bijective.

12:                                                     We introduce the concept of non-Archimedean metrics attached to a transcen-
13:                                                 dental pseudoeffective cohomology class on a compact Kähler manifold. This is
14:                                                 obtained via extending the Ross–Witt Nyström correspondence to the relative case,
15:                                                 and we point out that our construction agrees with that of Boucksom–Jonsson when
16:                                                 the class is induced by a pseudoeffective Q-line bundle.
17:                                                     We introduce the notion of a flag configuration attached to a transcendental big
18:                                                 class, recovering the notion of a test configuration in the ample case. We show that
19:                                                 non-Archimedean finite energy metrics are approximable by flag configurations, and
20:                                                 very general versions of the radial Ding energy are continuous, a novel result even
21:                                                 in the ample case. As applications, we characterize the delta invariant as the Ding
22:                                                 semistability threshold of flag configurations and filtrations, and prove a YTD type
23:                                                 existence theorem for Kähler–Einstein metrics in terms of flag configurations.

112:    When {θ} is the first Chern class of a Q-line bundle L, Boucksom and Jonsson defined
113: the space of non-Archimedean metrics PSHNA (Lan ) in [BJ21] using algebraic tools (see
114: Section 2.3). In our first result we show that our construction agrees with theirs in this
115: important particular case.
116: Theorem 1.1. (=Theorem 3.14) When {θ} is the first Chern class of a pseudoeffective
117: Q-line bundle L, there is a natural bijection between PSHNA (θ) and PSH(Lan ).
118:     The same holds for a pseudoeffective (1, 1)-class lying in the Néron–Severi group with
119: real coefficients, as we explain in Remark 3.15.
120:     For the construction of the natural map between PSHNA (θ) and PSH(Lan ), we refer
121: to (39). Recently Boucksom–Jonsson have showed that the so-called envelope conjecture

record.search_query: On a smooth projective variety and for a pseudoeffective real Neron-Severi class, full realized divisorial or b-divisor singularity data admits an all-mass order isomorphism, whereas a literal multiplier-ideal formula over all semivaluations is stated only for a rational line-bundle class.
search_evidence: The theorem search did not return the precise DXZ comparison. The pinned DXZ v3 primary source gives the projective pseudoeffective construction, the Q-line-bundle comparison map and order-preserving bijection, and explicitly notes its real Neron--Severi extension.

source_evidence.comparison: Lines 84--105 define I-maximal test curves, explain that individual MTCI spaces require positive mass after Kähler perturbation, and then form the projective-limit PSHNA(theta) for a pseudoeffective class. This is a distinct object from the scalar I-class of one potential in the target theorem.

Lines 873--886 define PSHNA(theta) for a pseudoeffective class as the inverse limit over Kähler perturbations and equip it with a componentwise partial order, confirming the full-object and all-mass framework referenced in the scope.

Lines 663--690 identify the Berkovich analytification of a projective variety with semivaluations on all irreducible subvarieties and distinguish the divisorial locus. This is the all-semivaluation target that the P14.8 theorem expressly does not reconstruct.

Lines 112--119 state the natural bijection for a pseudoeffective Q-line bundle and its extension to pseudoeffective real Neron--Severi classes. Lines 1174--1204 define the actual map to Boucksom--Jonsson functions under the Q-line-bundle hypothesis and state that the bijection preserves order in the needed direction.

record.contextual_definition_comparison: DXZ's PSHNA(theta) is a projective-limit family of I-maximal test curves and its Boucksom--Jonsson realization is a function on the full Berkovich semivaluation space. The theorem under review instead starts from the scalar, realizable tower of one theta-psh potential and selects only its canonical I-envelope representative; these domains and outputs are not identified.
record.applicability: The scope paragraph accurately leaves the DXZ/Boucksom--Jonsson comparison intact only in its smooth projective algebraic setting and does not use it to prove the compact-Kähler scalar theorem. The explicit all-semivaluation comparison map inspected here is introduced under a pseudoeffective Q-line-bundle hypothesis, with the real Neron--Severi extension stated separately.
record.detail: The source confirms that the excluded order-isomorphism reading is mathematically distinct and that the present proof makes no compact-Kähler or genuinely transcendental extension of the algebraic semivaluation comparison.

record.applicability: The scope paragraph accurately leaves the DXZ/Boucksom--Jonsson comparison intact only in its smooth projective algebraic setting and does not use it to prove the compact-Kähler scalar theorem. The explicit all-semivaluation comparison map inspected here is introduced under a pseudoeffective Q-line-bundle hypothesis, with the real Neron--Severi extension stated separately.
record.detail: The source confirms that the excluded order-isomorphism reading is mathematically distinct and that the present proof makes no compact-Kähler or genuinely transcendental extension of the algebraic semivaluation comparison.

record.detail: The ambient assumptions are: X is connected and compact Kähler; theta is a smooth closed real (1,1)-form; PSH(X,theta) is nonempty. The quotient ranges only over classes induced by actual theta-psh potentials, not formal ideal or valuative towers. The data are the full multiplier-ideal tower for every positive integer scaling, equivalently the complete divisorial generic-Lelong profile. R_theta is asserted only on this realizable quotient and targets the normalized I-envelope representative. No positivity of the nonpluripolar mass is assumed.
record.location: Statement opening paragraph and Theorem (P14.8 v5), definition of D_I and R_theta

record.detail: For an actual representative phi, compactness and upper semicontinuity make sup_X phi finite, and phi-sup_X phi is theta-psh, nonpositive, and has unchanged multiplier ideals, so F_d is nonempty. Finite maxima of theta-psh functions are theta-psh and remain nonpositive. At every prime divisor over X the generic Lelong number of a maximum is the minimum; because both inputs have the same profile d, the maximum has that same profile. The divisorial criterion therefore keeps the entire scaled multiplier-ideal tower fixed, so F_d is directed under finite maxima.
record.location: Proof, first paragraph defining F_d

record.detail: The family is locally uniformly bounded above by zero, so Choquet's lemma produces a countable subfamily whose supremum has the same usc regularization U. Finite successive maxima u_j stay in F_d, increase, and converge almost everywhere to U. For any fixed prime divisor E on a model, Lemma 10.5 permits one point of E outside the countable union of exceptional analytic sets for all pulled-back u_j and U. After adding a smooth local potential for the pulled-back theta, these are local psh functions; the increasing-limit Lelong theorem applies and yields nu_E(U)=lim_j nu_E(u_j)=nu(d,E). This argument is repeated for each E and does not require a single point working for uncountably many divisors.
record.location: Proof, paragraph beginning 'Put U' through equation nu(U,E)=lim_j nu(u_j,E)

record.detail: Equality of every divisorial Lelong number between U and d remains equality after each positive integral scaling. The valuative multiplier-ideal criterion then gives I(mU)=I(mphi) for every m>=1, hence [U]_I=d. Therefore U itself is a competitor and dominates every competitor by construction. Since the competitor family is defined solely from d, its largest member is independent of the chosen representative and is exactly the I-envelope P_theta[phi]_I; applying the same construction again is idempotent.
record.location: Proof, paragraph beginning 'Apply the valuative multiplier-ideal criterion'

record.detail: Because U<=0, sup_X U<=0. If the supremum were negative, adding a sufficiently small positive constant would preserve theta-psh status and every multiplier ideal while retaining the inequality <=0, producing a strictly larger competitor; hence sup_X U=0. A normalized I-model in d is, by the I-model fixed-point definition, the largest element of this same competitor family, so it equals U. This proves existence, normalization, and uniqueness without a mass condition.
record.location: Proof, end of first-assertion argument: normalization and uniqueness

record.detail: With ell_0=1 and ell_m=exp(-4^m), the child-fitting inequalities 2 ell_1<ell_0 and 2 ell_{m+1}/ell_m=2 exp(-3*4^m)<1 hold, so two children of the prescribed next length fit at every stage. Assigning mass 2^-m to each stage-m interval gives a consistent limiting probability measure. Any singleton lies in nested stage intervals whose masses tend to zero, so the measure is nonatomic. The capacity series has terms 2^-m log(1/ell_m)=2^m for m>=1 and diverges; the cited generalized-Cantor criterion therefore makes the compact support F logarithmic-capacity zero, hence polar and pluripolar on P^1. Rescaling the initial circumference changes no convergence conclusion.
record.location: Proof, generalized Cantor construction through the zero-capacity conclusion

record.detail: For normalized Fubini--Study area one, the normalized Green potential G_p exists with omega+dd^c G_p=delta_p and sup G_p=0. Integrating this kernel against the probability measure mu is legitimate as an extended psh construction. At any point outside the compact support F, positive distance from F bounds the kernel uniformly below, while normalization bounds it above, so G_mu is not identically minus infinity. Linearity/Fubini in currents gives omega+dd^c G_mu=mu. Thus phi_s=sG_mu is omega-psh for 0<=s<=1 and omega+dd^c phi_s=(1-s)omega+s mu.
record.location: Proof, paragraph defining G_p, G_mu, and phi_s

record.detail: On a smooth Riemann surface the Lelong number of a positive (1,1)-current at a point equals its atomic mass there. Both omega and the constructed mu are nonatomic, so every point Lelong number of phi_s is zero. Prime divisors over a smooth curve give only point divisorial valuations; hence every divisorial Lelong number also vanishes. After every integral scaling m the profile still vanishes, and the valuative membership criterion puts 1 in I(m phi_s), proving I(m phi_s)=O_X for all m>=1 and [phi_s]_I=[0]_I.
record.location: Proof, paragraph on Lelong numbers and scaled multiplier ideals

record.detail: The measure mu is supported on F. On X\F the Green potential is locally bounded (indeed its kernel is smooth away from the support), so plurifine locality identifies the degree-one nonpluripolar product there with the ordinary current, namely (1-s)omega. Nonpluripolar products put no mass on the pluripolar set F, and the smooth measure omega also gives F zero mass. Consequently the product is globally (1-s)omega and its total mass is 1-s.
record.location: Proof, BEGZ degree-one calculation and equations for the nonpluripolar mass

record.detail: All phi_s lie in the realizable trivial I-class, so the first assertion gives the common canonical normalized model 0. At s=1 the raw product mass is zero, whereas the model 0 has mass integral_X omega=1; varying s also exhibits every mass in [0,1] inside the same class. This proves failure of reconstruction for a raw representative and its raw mass. The proof never realizes arbitrary formal data, never asserts an all-semivaluation reconstruction formula, never invokes the separate projective all-mass order isomorphism outside its Neron--Severi setting, and does not use the P14.7 terminal-left-limit corollary. The stated exclusions therefore match the actual scope.
record.location: Proof, final paragraph and Statement Scope paragraph
